text: Lumber Grades

label: Sentence
text: Except for joists, rafters, trusses and beams, visually graded lumber shall conform to the grades in Table 9.3.2.1. (See Article 9.23.4.2. for joists, rafters and beams and Article 9.23.14.11. for trusses.)

label: Article
text: Machine Stress Rated Lumber

label: Sentence
text: Machine stress rated lumber shall conform to the requirements of Subsection 4.3.1.

label: Article
text: OSB, Waferboard and Plywood Marking

label: Sentence
text: OSB, waferboard and plywood used for roof sheathing, wall sheathing and subflooring shall be legibly identified on the face of the material indicating

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the manufacturer of the material,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the standard to which it is produced, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: that the material is of an exterior type.

label: Article
text: Moisture Content

label: Sentence
text: Moisture content of lumber shall be not more than 19% at the time of installation.

label: Article
text: Lumber Dimensions

label: Sentence
text: Lumber dimensions referred to in this Part are actual dimensions determined in conformance with CSA O141, “Softwood Lumber.”

label: Article
text: Panel Thickness Tolerances

label: Sentence
text: The thicknesses specified in this Part for plywood, hardboard, particleboard, OSB and waferboard shall be subject to the tolerances permitted in the standards referenced for these products unless specifically indicated herein.

label: Article
text: Undersized Lumber

label: Sentence
text: Joist, rafter, lintel and beam members up to 5% less than the actual Canadian standard sizes are permitted to be used provided the allowable spans for the grade and species of lumber under consideration are reduced 5% from those shown in the Span Tables for full size members. (See Note A-9.3.2.8.(1).)

label: Article
text: Termite and Decay Protection

label: Sentence
text: In localities where termites are known to occur,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: clearance between structural wood elements and the finished ground level directly below them shall be not less than 450 mm and, except as provided in Sentence (2), all sides of the supporting elements shall be visible to permit inspection, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: structural wood elements, supported by elements in contact with the ground or exposed over bare soil, shall be pressure-treated with a chemical that is toxic to termites.

label: Sentence
text: In localities where termites are known to occur and foundations are insulated or otherwise finished in a manner that could conceal a termite infestation,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: a metal or plastic barrier shall be installed through the insulation and any other separation or finish materials above finished ground level to control the passage of termites behind or through the insulation, separation or finish materials, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: all sides of the finished supporting assembly shall be visible to permit inspection.

label: Sentence
text: Structural wood elements shall be pressure-treated with a preservative to resist decay,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: where the vertical clearance between structural wood elements and the finished ground level is less than 150 mm (see also Articles 9.23.2.2. and 9.23.2.3.), or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: where

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: the wood elements are not protected from exposure to precipitation,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: the configuration is conducive to moisture accumulation, and

label: Subclause
title: iii)
text: the moisture index is greater than 1.00.

label: Sentence
text: Structural wood elements used in retaining walls and cribbing shall be pressure-treated with a preservative to resist decay, where

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the retaining wall or cribbing supports ground that is critical to the stability of building foundations , or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the retaining wall or cribbing is greater than 1.2 m in height.

label: Sentence
text: Where wood is required by this Article to be treated to resist termites or decay, such treatment shall be in accordance with Table 2, Use Categories for Specific Products, Uses, and Exposures, of CAN/CSA-O80.1, “Specification of treated wood,” as follows:

label: Clause
title: a)
text: Use Category 1 (UC1), where the wood member is used in

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: interior construction,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: above-ground applications, and

label: Clause
title: iii) applications where the wood member remains dry,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: Use Category 2 (UC2), where the wood member is used in

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: interior construction,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: above-ground applications, and

label: Subclause
title: iii)
text: applications where the wood member may be subjected to occasional sources of moisture,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: Use Category 3.2 (UC3.2), where the wood member is used in

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: exterior construction,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: above-ground applications, and

label: Clause
title: iii) applications where the wood member is uncoated or is used
text: in a configuration conducive to moisture accumulation,

label: Clause
title: d)
text: Use Category 4.1 (UC4.1), where

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: the wood member is in contact with the ground,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: the wood member is in contact with fresh water, or

label: Clause
title: iii) the vertical clearance between the wood element and the
text: finished ground level is less than 150 mm and the wood elements are not separated from permeable supporting materials by a moisture barrier, or

label: Clause
title: e)
text: Use Category 4.2 (UC4.2), where the wood member is used in critical structural components, including permanent wood foundations .

label: Sentence
text: Where wood is protected in accordance with UC1 or UC2 using an inorganic boron preservative, the wood shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: protected from direct exposure to water during and after the completion of construction, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: separated from permeable supporting materials by a moisture barrier that is resistant to all expected mechanisms of deterioration in the service environment if the vertical clearance to the ground is less than 150 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Wood that is required by this Article to be treated to resist termites or decay shall be identified by a mark to indicate the type of preservative used and conformance to the relevant required Use Category.

label: Subsection
text: Metal

label: Article
text: Sheet Metal Thickness

label: Sentence
text: Minimum thicknesses for sheet metal material that are stated in this Part refer to the actual minimum base metal thicknesses measured at any point of the material and, in the case of galvanized steel described in Sentence 9.3.3.2.(1), include the thickness of the galvanizing coating unless otherwise indicated.

label: Article
text: Galvanized Sheet Steel

label: Sentence
text: Where sheet steel is required to be galvanized, it shall be metallic-coated with zinc or an alloy of 55% aluminum-zinc meeting the requirements of

label: Clause
title: a)
text: ASTM A653/A653M, “Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, Zinc-Coated (Galvanized) or Zinc-Iron Alloy-Coated (Galvannealed) by the Hot-Dip Process,” or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: ASTM A792/A792M, “Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, 55% Aluminum-Zinc Alloy-Coated by the Hot-Dip Process.”

label: Sentence
text: Where galvanized sheet steel is intended for use in locations exposed to the weather or as a flashing material, it shall have a zinc coating not less than the G90 [Z275] coating designation or an aluminum-zinc alloy coating not less than the AZM150 coating designation, as referred to in Sentence (1).

label: Section
title: Section 9.4.
text: Structural Requirements

label: Subsection
text: Structural Design Requirements and Application Limitations

label: Article
text: General

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.4.1.1.)

label: Sentence
text: Subject to the application limitations defined elsewhere in this Part, structural members and their connections shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: conform to requirements provided elsewhere in this Part,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: be designed according to good engineering practice such as that provided in CWC 2014, “Engineering Guide for Wood Frame Construction,” or

label: Clause
title: c)
text: be designed according to Part 4 using the loads and deflection and vibration limits specified in

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: Part 9, or

label: Sentence
text: Where floor framing is designed in accordance with Clause (1)(b) or (c), and where supporting wall framing and fastenings, or footings are designed according to Clause (1)(a), the maximum specified live load on the floor according to Table 4.1.5.3. shall not exceed 2.4 kPa.

references.link_text: Live load means a variable load due to the intended use and occupancy that is to be assumed in the design of the structural members of a building . It includes loads due to cranes and the pressure of liquids in containers.

label: Sentence
text: Location-specific information for structural design, including snow and wind loads and seismic spectral accelerations, shall be determined according to Subsection 1.1.3.

label: Subsection
text: Specified Loads

label: Article
text: Application

label: Sentence
text: This Subsection applies to light-frame constructions whose wall, floor and roof planes are generally comprised of frames of small repetitive structural members, and where

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the roof and wall planes are clad, sheathed or braced on at least one side,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the small repetitive structural members are spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: the clear span of any structural member does not exceed 12.2 m,

label: Clause
title: d)
text: the maximum deflection of the structural roof members conforms to Article 9.4.3.1.,

label: Clause
title: e)
text: the maximum total roof area, notwithstanding any separation of adjoining buildings by firewalls , is 4 550 m 2 , and

label: Clause
title: f)
text: for flat roofs, there are no significant obstructions on the roof, such as parapet walls, spaced closer than the distance calculated by where D o = minimum distance between obstructions, m, H o = height of the obstruction above the roof, m, S s = ground snow load, kPa, and γ = specific weight of snow taken as 4.0 kN/m 3 or 0.43S s + 2.2 kN/m 3 , whichever is lesser.

label: Article
text: Specified Snow Loads

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) to (4), specified snow loads shall be not less than those calculated using the following formula: where S = specified snow load, C b = basic snow load roof factor, which is 0.45 where the entire width of the roof does not exceed 4.3 m and 0.55 for all other roofs, S s = 1-in-50-year ground snow load in kPa, determined according to Subsection 1.1.3., and S r = associated 1-in-50-year rain load in kPa, determined according to Subsection 1.1.3.

label: Sentence
text: In no case shall the specified snow load be less than 1 kPa.

label: Sentence
text: Bow string, arch or semi-circular roof trusses having an unsupported span greater than 6 m shall be designed in conformance with the snow load requirements in Subsection 4.1.6.

label: Sentence
text: Where the height of a roof step at the intersection of an upper level roof and a lower level roof is greater than 2 m, and the upper level roof has a slope less than 1 in 6 and an area greater than 600 m 2 , the specified snow load on the lower level roof shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: for distances from the roof step that are less than or equal to the drift length, x d , calculated in accordance with Sentence (5), not less than 1.5 times the specified snow load, S, calculated using the formula in Sentence (1) with C b equal to 0.55, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: for distances from the roof step that are greater than the drift length, x d , calculated in accordance with Sentence (5), as specified in Sentence (1).

label: Sentence
text: For the purposes of Sentence (4), the drift length, x d , in m, shall be calculated as follows: where h = height of the roof step, in m, and γ = specific weight of snow as specified in Clause 9.4.2.1.(1)(f).

label: Article
text: Platforms Subject to Snow and Occupancy Loads

label: Sentence
text: Balconies, decks and other accessible exterior platforms intended for an occupancy and subject to snow loads shall be designed to carry the specified roof snow load or 1.9 kPa, whichever is greater, where the platform, or each segregated area of the platform, serves a single dwelling unit . (See Note A-9.4.2.3.(1).)

references.link_text: Occupancy means the use or intended use of a building or part thereof for the shelter or support of persons, animals or property.
Dwelling unit means a suite operated as a housekeeping unit, used or intended to be used by one or more persons and usually containing cooking, eating, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities.

label: Article
text: Attics and Roof Spaces

label: Sentence
text: The ceiling joists or truss bottom chords in residential attic or roof spaces having limited accessibility that precludes the storage of equipment or material shall be designed for a total specified load of not less than 0.35 kPa, where the total specified load is the sum of the specified dead load plus the specified live load of the ceiling. (See Note A-9.4.2.4.(1).)

references.link_text: Dead load means the weight of all permanent structural and non-structural components of a building .

Live load means a variable load due to the intended use and occupancy that is to be assumed in the design of the structural members of a building . It includes loads due to cranes and the pressure of liquids in containers.

title: Section 9.5.
text: Design of Areas and Spaces

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Method of Measurement

label: Sentence
text: Unless otherwise indicated herein, dimensions of rooms or spaces shall be measured between finished wall surfaces and between finished floor and ceiling surfaces.

label: Article
text: Combination Rooms

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.5.1.2.)

label: Sentence

label: Article
text: Types of Glazing and Protection of Glazing

label: Sentence
text: Glass sidelights greater than 500 mm wide that could be mistaken for doors, glass in storm doors and glass in sliding doors within or at every entrance to a dwelling unit and in public areas shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: safety glazing of the tempered or laminated type conforming to CAN/CGSB-12.1, “Safety Glazing,” or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: wired glass conforming to CAN/CGSB-12.11-M, “Wired Safety Glass.”

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (4), glass in entrance doors to dwelling units and in public areas, other than the entrance doors described in Sentence (1), shall be safety glazing or wired glass of the type described in Sentence (1) where the glass area exceeds 0.5 m 2 and extends to less than 900 mm from the bottom of the door.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (4), transparent panels that could be mistaken as a means of egress shall be protected by barriers or railings.

references.link_text: Means of egress means a continuous path of travel provided for the escape of persons from any point in a building or contained open space to a separate building , an open public thoroughfare, or an exterior open space protected from fire exposure from the building and having access to an open public thoroughfare. Means of egress includes exits and access to exits .

label: Sentence
text: Sliding glass partitions that separate a public corridor from an adjacent occupancy and that are open during normal working hours need not conform to Sentences (2), (3) and (5), except that such partitions shall be suitably marked to indicate their existence and position.

references.link_text: Public corridor means a corridor that provides access to exit from more than one suite .
Occupancy means the use or intended use of a building or part thereof for the shelter or support of persons, animals or property.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (4), every glass or transparent door accessible to the public shall be equipped with hardware, bars or other permanent fixtures designed so that the existence and position of such doors is readily apparent.

label: Sentence
text: Glazing used for a shower or bathtub enclosure shall conform to Class A of CAN/CGSB-12.1, “Safety Glazing.”

text: For the purpose of this Section, the term “doors” includes glazing in doors and sidelights for doors.

text: Heat Transfer Performance

label: Clause
title: a)

label: Clause
title: b)
text: ensure comfortable conditions for occupants.

label: Sentence
text: Compliance with the heat transfer performance requirements described in Sentence (1) shall be demonstrated by

label: Clause
title: a)

label: Clause
title: b)

label: Article
text: Thermal Characteristics of Windows, Doors and Skylights

label: Sentence
text: Metal frames and sash of windows, doors and skylights shall incorporate a thermal break.

label: Sentence
text: Windows and doors described in Sentence (1) do not require a thermal break where they are installed as

label: Clause
title: a)
text: vehicular access doors,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: storm windows and doors, or

label: Clause
title: c)
text: windows and doors that are required to have a fire-resistance rating .

text: Application

label: Sentence
text: This Subsection applies to windows, doors and skylights covered in the scope of AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440, “North American Fenestration Standard/Specification for windows, doors, and skylights” (Harmonized Standard).

text: General

label: Clause

title: d)

label: Article
text: Performance Requirements

label: Sentence
text: Performance grades for windows, doors and skylights shall be selected according to the Canadian Supplement referenced in Clause 9.7.4.2.(1)(b) so as to be appropriate for the conditions and geographic location in which the window, door or skylight will be installed.

label: Sentence
text: Windows, doors and skylights shall conform to the performance grades selected in Sentence (1) when tested in accordance with the Harmonized Standard referenced in Clause 9.7.4.2.(1)(a).

label: Sentence
text: The minimum level of performance required for windows, doors and skylights shall be that of the Performance Class R.

label: Sentence
text: Exterior wood doors shall conform to CAN/CSA-O132.2 Series, “Wood Flush Doors,” and shall have legibly indicated on them

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the name of the manufacturer,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the standard according to which they were produced, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: that they are of an exterior type.

label: Clause

text: Glass for site-built windows, doors, sidelights for doors, and skylights shall comply with Section 9.6.

label: Article
text: Resistance to Forced Entry for Doors

label: Clause

text: swinging entrance doors to dwelling units ,

label: Clause
title: b)

label: Clause
title: c)
text: swinging doors that provide access directly or indirectly from a storage garage to a dwelling unit .

label: Sentence
text: Doors, frames and hardware that conform to a security level of at least Grade 10 as described in the Annex to ASTM F476, “Standard Test Methods for Security of Swinging Door Assemblies,” are not required to conform to Sentences (3) to (7). (See Note A-9.7.5.2.(2).)

label: Clause

text: be solid core or stile-and-rail type,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: be not less than 45 mm thick, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: if of the stile-and-rail type, have a panel thickness of not less than 19 mm, with a total panel area not more than half of the door area.

label: Sentence

label: Clause

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Article 9.9.6.7.)

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), an inactive leaf in double doors used in locations specified in Sentence (1) shall be provided with heavy-duty bolts top and bottom having an engagement of not less than 15 mm.

label: Sentence

label: Clause
title: a)
text: to wood doors with wood screws not less than 25 mm long and to wood frames with wood screws so that at least 2 screws per hinge penetrate not less than 30 mm into solid wood, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: to metal doors and metal frames with machine screws not smaller than No. 10 and not less than 10 mm long.

label: Sentence

label: Clause
title: a)
text: to wood frames with wood screws that penetrate not less than 30 mm into solid wood, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: to metal frames with machine screws not smaller than No. 8 and not less than 10 mm long.

label: Sentence
text: Except for storm or screen doors, doors described in Sentence (1) that swing outward shall be provided with hinges or pins so that the doors cannot be removed when they are in the closed position. (See Note A-9.7.5.2.(8).)

label: Sentence

label: Article
text: Resistance to Forced Entry for Windows

label: Sentence
text: In dwelling units , windows, any part of which is located within 2 m of adjacent ground level, shall conform to the requirements for resistance to forced entry as described in Clause 5.3.6 of AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440, “North American Fenestration Standard/Specification for windows, doors, and skylights.” (See Note A-9.7.5.3.(1).)

label: Subsection
text: Installation

label: Article
text: Installation of Windows, Doors and Skylights

label: Sentence
text: The installation of windows, doors and skylights shall conform to CSA A440.4, “Window, door, and skylight installation,” except that

label: Clause
title: a)
text: shims used to support windows, doors and skylights are permitted to be made of treated plywood, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: protection from precipitation for walls incorporating windows or doors and for roofs incorporating skylights, and the interfaces of these walls with windows or doors and of roofs with skylights, shall also conform to

label: Sentence
text: The installation of manufactured and pre-assembled windows, doors and skylights and the field assembly of manufactured window and door combination units shall conform to the manufacturer's instructions.

label: Sentence
text: Windows, doors and skylights shall be sealed to air barriers.

label: Article
text: Sealants, Trim and Flashing

label: Sentence
text: The sealing compound used to seal the glass component of an insulating glazing unit to the sash component shall be compatible with the sealing compound used to edge seal the glass component.

label: Sentence
text: Flashing used to protect openings shall conform to Articles 9.27.3.7. and 9.27.3.8.

label: Sentence
text: Sealants shall be applied between window frames or trim and the exterior cladding or masonry in conformance with Subsection 9.27.4.

label: Sentence
text: All unfinished portions of the frame and other components of aluminum windows, doors or skylights in contact with the edges of masonry, concrete, stucco or plaster shall be protected with an alkali-resistant coating.

label: Sentence
text: This Section applies to the design and construction of interior and exterior stairs, steps, ramps , handrails and guards .

label: Article
text: Stairs, Ramps, Landings, Handrails and Guards in Garages

label: Sentence
text: Where stairs, ramps , landings, handrails or guards are installed in garages that serve a single dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite including their common spaces, the garage shall be considered to be part of the dwelling unit and the requirements for stairs, ramps , landings, handrails and guards within dwelling units shall apply.

references.link_text: Dwelling unit means a suite operated as a housekeeping unit, used or intended to be used by one or more persons and usually containing cooking, eating, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities.

Secondary suite means a self-contained dwelling unit located in a building or portion of a building of only residential occupancy that contains only one other dwelling unit and common spaces, and where both dwelling units constitute a single real estate entity. (See Note A-1.4.1.2.(1).) Semi-public swimming pool means a swimming pool

label: Section
title: Section 9.16.
text: Floors-on-Ground

label: Subsection
text: Scope

label: Article
text: Application

label: Sentence
text: This Section applies to floors supported on ground or on granular fill that do not provide structural support for the superstructure.

label: Article
text: Structural Floors

label: Sentence
text: Floors-on-ground that support loads from the superstructure shall be designed in conformance with Part 4.

label: Article
text: Required Floors-on-Ground

label: Sentence
text: All spaces within dwelling units , except crawl spaces, shall be provided with a floor-on-ground, where

label: Clause
title: a)
text: access is provided to the space, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: a floor supported by the structure is not provided.

label: Article
text: Dampproofing and Waterproofing

label: Sentence
text: Dampproofing and waterproofing shall conform to Section 9.13.

label: Subsection
text: Material beneath Floors

label: Article
text: Required Installation of Granular Material

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve shall be placed beneath floors-on-ground. (See also Subsection 9.13.4. and Note A-9.13.4.)

label: Sentence
text: Granular material need not be installed under

label: Clause
title: a)
text: slabs in garages, carports or accessory buildings , or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: buildings of industrial occupancy where the nature of the process contained therein permits or requires the use of large openings in the building envelope even during the winter.

references.link_text: Industrial occupancy (Group F) means the occupancy or use of a building or part thereof for the assembling, fabricating, manufacturing, processing, repairing or storing of goods and materials.

building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Article
text: Support of Floors

label: Sentence
text: Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to variations in moisture content or chemical-microbiological oxidation shall not be used as fill beneath floors-on-ground in a concentration that will damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See also Article 9.4.4.4. and Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Sentence
text: Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to freezing shall not be used as fill beneath floors-on-ground that will be subjected to freezing temperatures.

label: SeeAlso

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (4), fill beneath floors-on-ground shall be compacted.

label: Sentence
text: Fill beneath floors-on-ground need not be compacted where the material is clean coarse aggregate containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

label: Subsection
text: Drainage

label: Article
text: Control of Water Ingress

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Article 9.16.3.2. or where it can be shown to be unnecessary, ingress of water underneath a floor-on-ground shall be prevented by grading or drainage.

text: Hydrostatic Pressure

label: Sentence
text: Where groundwater levels may cause hydrostatic pressure beneath a floor-on-ground, the floor-on-ground shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: a poured concrete slab, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: designed to resist such pressures.

label: Article
text: Floor Drains

label: Sentence
text: When floor drains are required (see Section 9.31.), the floor surface shall be sloped so that no water can accumulate.

label: Subsection
text: Concrete

label: Article
text: Surface Finish

label: Sentence
text: The finished surface of concrete floor slabs shall be trowelled smooth and even.

label: Sentence
text: Dry cement shall not be added to the floor surfaces to absorb surplus water.

label: Article
text: Topping Course

label: Sentence
text: When a topping course is provided for a concrete floor slab, it shall consist of 1 part cement to 2.5 parts clean, well graded sand by volume, with a water/cement ratio approximately equal to that of the base slab.

label: Sentence
text: When concrete topping is provided, it shall not be less than 20 mm thick.

label: Article
text: Thickness

label: Sentence
text: Concrete slabs shall not be less than 75 mm thick exclusive of concrete topping.

label: Article
text: Bond Break

label: Sentence
text: A bond-breaking material shall be placed between the slab and footings or rock .

label: Subsection
text: Wood

label: Article
text: Wood-Frame Floors

label: Sentence
text: Floors-on-ground constructed of wood shall conform to CSA S406, “Specification of permanent wood foundations for housing and small buildings.”

label: Section
title: Section 9.17.
text: Columns

label: Subsection
text: Scope

label: Article
text: Application

label: Sentence
text: This Section applies to columns used to support

label: Clause
title: a)
text: beams carrying loads from not more than 2 wood-frame floors where

label: Subclause
title: i)

title: ii) the
text: live load on any floor does not exceed 2.4 kPa (see

label: Clause
title: b)
text: beams or header joists carrying loads from not more than 2 levels of wood-frame balconies, decks or other accessible exterior platforms, or 1 level plus the roof, where

label: Subclause
title: i)

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: the sum of the specified snow and occupancy loads does not exceed 4.8 kPa (see Sentence 9.4.2.3.(1) for the determination of load on platform-type constructions), and

label: Subclause
title: iii)
text: the platform serves only a single suite of residential occupancy , or

label: Clause
title: c)
text: carport roofs (see Section 9.35.).

label: Sentence
text: Columns for applications other than as described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in accordance with Part 4.

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Location

label: Sentence
text: Columns shall be centrally located on a footing conforming to Section 9.15.

label: Article
text: Lateral Support

label: Sentence
text: Columns shall be securely fastened to the supported member to reduce the likelihood of lateral differential movement between the column and the supported member. (See also Article 9.23.6.2.)

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted by Sentence (3), columns shall be laterally supported to resist racking

label: Clause
title: a)
text: directly, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: by connection to the supported members.

label: Sentence
text: Columns need not be provided with lateral support as described in Sentence (2), where

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists is not more than 600 mm, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the columns support a deck with no superstructure.

label: Subsection
text: Steel Columns

label: Article
text: Size and Thickness

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), steel pipe columns shall have an outside diameter of not less than 73 mm and a wall thickness of not less than 4.76 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Columns of sizes other than as specified in Sentence (1) are permitted to be used where the loadbearing capacities are shown to be adequate.

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Article
text: End Bearing Plates

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), steel columns shall be fitted with not less than 100 mm by 100 mm by 6.35 mm thick steel plates at each end, and where the column supports a wooden beam, the top plate shall extend across the full width of the beam.

label: Sentence
text: The top plate required in Sentence (1) need not be provided where a column supports a steel beam and provision is made for the attachment of the column to the beam.

label: Article
text: Paint

label: Sentence
text: Exterior steel columns shall be treated on the outside surface with at least one coat of rust-inhibitive paint.

label: Article
text: Design of Steel Columns

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.17.3.4.)

label: Sentence
text: Where the imposed load does not exceed 36 kN, adjustable steel columns shall conform to CAN/CGSB-7.2, “Adjustable Steel Columns.”

label: Sentence
text: Steel columns other than those described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in accordance with Part 4.

label: Subsection
text: Wood Columns

label: Article
text: Column Sizes

label: Sentence
text: The width or diameter of a wood column shall be not less than the width of the supported member.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Article 9.35.4.2., columns shall be not less than 184 mm for round columns and 140 mm by 140 mm for rectangular columns, unless calculations are provided to show that lesser sizes are adequate.

label: Article
text: Materials

label: Sentence
text: Wood columns shall be either solid, glued-laminated or built-up.

label: Sentence
text: Built-up columns shall consist of not less than 38 mm thick full-length members

label: Clause
title: a)
text: bolted together with not less than 9.52 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 450 mm o.c., or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: nailed together with not less than 76 mm nails spaced not more than 300 mm o.c.

label: Sentence
text: Glued-laminated columns shall conform to Section 4.3.

label: Article
text: Columns in Contact with Concrete

label: Sentence
text: Wood columns shall be separated from concrete in contact with the ground by 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.

label: Subsection
text: Unit Masonry Columns

label: Article
text: Materials

label: Sentence
text: Unit masonry columns shall be built of masonry units

label: Clause
title: a)
text: conforming to CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units,” and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: having a compressive strength over the net area of the block of not less than 15 MPa.

label: Article
text: Sizes

label: Sentence
text: Unit masonry columns shall be not less than 290 mm by 290 mm or 240 mm by 380 mm in size.

label: Subsection
text: Solid Concrete Columns

label: Article
text: Materials

label: Sentence
text: Concrete shall conform to Section 9.3.

label: Article
text: Sizes

label: Sentence
text: Concrete columns shall be not less than 200 mm by 200 mm for rectangular columns and 230 mm diam for circular columns.

label: Section
title: Section 9.18.
text: Crawl Spaces

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Application

label: Sentence
text: This Section applies to crawl spaces whose exterior walls have less than 25% of their total area above exterior ground level open to the outdoors.

label: Article
text: Foundations

label: Sentence
text: Foundations enclosing crawl spaces shall conform to Section 9.15.

label: Article
text: Heated and Unheated Crawl Spaces

label: Sentence
text: Crawl spaces shall be considered to be heated where the space

label: Clause
title: a)
text: is used as a hot air plenum ,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: contains heating ducts that are not sealed and insulated to minimize heat loss to the space, or

label: Clause
title: c)
text: is not separated from heated space in accordance with Section 9.25.

label: Sentence
text: Heating of heated crawl spaces shall conform to Section 9.33.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation, an air barrier system and a vapour barrier shall be installed in the walls of heated crawl spaces in accordance with Section 9.25.

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Subsection
text: Access

label: Article
text: Access Openings

label: Sentence
text: An access opening of not less than 500 mm by 700 mm shall be provided to each crawl space where the crawl space serves a single dwelling unit , and not less than 550 mm by 900 mm for other crawl spaces.

references.link_text: Dwelling unit means a suite operated as a housekeeping unit, used or intended to be used by one or more persons and usually containing cooking, eating, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities.

label: Sentence
text: Access openings shall be fitted with a door or hatch, except when the crawl space is heated and the access opening into the crawl space is from an adjacent heated space.

label: Subsection
text: Ventilation

label: Article
text: Ventilation of Unheated Crawl Spaces

label: Sentence
text: Unheated crawl spaces shall be ventilated by natural or mechanical means.

label: Sentence
text: Where an unheated crawl space is ventilated by natural means, ventilation shall be provided to the outside air by not less than 0.1 m 2 of unobstructed vent area for every 50 m 2 of floor area .

label: Sentence
text: Vents shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: uniformly distributed on opposite sides of the building , and

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: designed to prevent the entry of snow, rain and insects.

label: Article
text: Ventilation of Heated Crawl Spaces

label: Sentence
text: Heated crawl spaces shall be ventilated in accordance with Section 9.32.

label: Subsection
text: Clearance

label: SeeAlso
text: (See also Article 9.3.2.9.)

label: Article
text: Access Way to Services

label: Sentence
text: Where equipment requiring service such as plumbing cleanouts, traps and burners is located in crawl spaces, an access way with a height and width of not less than 600 mm shall be provided from the access door to the equipment and for a distance of 900 mm on the side or sides of the equipment to be serviced.

label: Subsection
text: Drainage

label: Article
text: Drainage

label: Sentence
text: Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, the ingress of water into a crawl space shall be controlled by grading or drainage.

label: Sentence
text: Drainage of foundation walls shall conform to Article 9.14.2.1.

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

label: Sentence
text: Drainage of the ground cover or floor-on-ground in the crawl space shall conform to Subsection 9.16.3.

label: Sentence
text: Drains shall conform to Section 9.14.

label: Subsection
text: Ground Cover

label: Article
text: Ground Cover in Unheated Crawl Spaces

label: Sentence
text: Where a crawl space is unheated, a ground cover shall be provided consisting of not less than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 50 mm of asphalt,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 100 mm of 15 MPa Portland cement concrete,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: Type S roll roofing, or

label: Clause
title: d)
text: 0.10 mm polyethylene.

label: Sentence
text: Joints in sheet-type ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be lapped not less than 100 mm and weighted down.

label: Article
text: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces

label: Sentence
text: Where a crawl space is heated, a ground cover consisting of not less than 0.15 mm polyethylene sheet conforming to CAN/CGSB-51.34-M, “Vapour Barrier, Polyethylene Sheet for Use in Building Construction,” shall be installed as part of an air barrier system in accordance with Subsection 9.25.3.

label: Sentence
text: The ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall have its joints lapped not less than 300 mm, and

label: Clause
title: a)
text: be sealed and evenly weighted down, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: be covered with concrete not less than 50 mm thick.

label: Sentence
text: The perimeter of the ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be sealed to the foundation wall. (See Notes A-9.13.4., A-9.25.3.4. and 9.25.3.6., and A-9.25.3.6.(2) and (3).)

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

label: Sentence
text: All penetrations of the ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be sealed against air leakage. (See Subsection 9.25.3.)

label: Subsection
text: Fire Protection

label: Article
text: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums

label: Sentence
text: Only crawl spaces under 1- storey portions of dwelling units shall be used as warm-air plenums .

references.link_text: Storey means that portion of a building that is situated between the top of any floor and the top of the floor next above it, and if there is no floor above it, that portion between the top of such floor and the ceiling above it.

label: Sentence
text: Enclosing material in crawl spaces described in Sentence (1), including insulation, shall have a surface flame-spread rating not greater than 150.

references.link_text: Flame-spread rating means an index or classification indicating the extent of spread-of-flame on the surface of a material or an assembly of materials as determined in a standard fire test as prescribed in this Code.

label: Sentence
text: Combustible ground cover in crawl spaces described in Sentence (1) shall be protected beneath each register opening with noncombustible material.

references.link_text: Combustible means that a material fails to meet the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Combustible construction means that type of construction that does not meet the requirements for noncombustible construction or encapsulated mass timber construction .

Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Sentence
text: The noncombustible register protection described in Sentence (3) shall

references.link_text: Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Clause
title: a)
text: extend not less than 300 mm beyond the projection of the register opening, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: have up-turned edges.

label: Section
title: Section 9.19.
text: Roof Spaces

label: Subsection
text: Venting

label: Article
text: Required Venting

label: Sentence
text: Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, where insulation is installed between a ceiling and the underside of the roof sheathing, a space shall be provided between the insulation and the sheathing, and vents shall be installed to permit the transfer of moisture from the space to the exterior. (See Note A-9.19.1.1.(1).)

label: Article
text: Vent Requirements

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/300 of the insulated ceiling area.

label: Sentence
text: Where the roof slope is less than 1 in 6 or in roofs that are constructed with roof joists, the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/150 of the insulated ceiling area.

label: Sentence
text: Required vents may be roof type, eave type, gable-end type or any combination thereof, and shall be distributed

label: Clause
title: a)
text: uniformly on opposite sides of the building ,

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the top of the space, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the bottom of the space.

label: Sentence
text: Except where each joist space is separately vented, roof joist spaces shall be interconnected by installing purlins not less than 38 mm by 38 mm on the top of the roof joists.

label: Sentence
text: Vents shall comply with CAN3-A93-M, “Natural Airflow Ventilators for Buildings.”

label: Article
text: Clearances

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), not less than 63 mm of space shall be provided between the top of the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing.

label: Sentence
text: At the junction of sloped roofs and exterior walls, where preformed baffles are used to contain the insulation, the baffles shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: provide an unobstructed air space, between the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing, that is

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: not less than 25 mm in dimension, and

label: Clause
title: ii) of sufficient cross area to meet the
text: attic or roof space venting requirements of Article 9.19.1.2., and

references.link_text: Attic or roof space means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

label: Clause
title: b)
text: extend vertically not less than 50 mm above the top of the insulation.

label: Sentence
text: Ceiling insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not restrict the free flow of air through roof vents or through any portion of the attic or roof space .

references.link_text: Attic or roof space means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

label: Article
text: Mansard or Gambrel Roof

label: Sentence
text: The lower portion of a mansard or gambrel style roof need not be ventilated.

label: Sentence
text: The upper portion of roofs described in Sentence (1) shall be ventilated in conformance with Articles 9.19.1.1. to 9.19.1.3.

label: Subsection
text: Access

label: Article
text: Access

label: Sentence
text: Every attic or roof space shall be provided with an access hatch where the open space in the attic or roof space measures

Attic or roof space means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

title: a)

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 1 m or more in length or width, and

label: Sentence
text: The hatch required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 550 mm by 900 mm except that, where the hatch serves not more than one dwelling unit , the hatch may be reduced to 0.32 m 2 in area with no dimension less than 500 mm.

references.link_text: Dwelling unit means a suite operated as a housekeeping unit, used or intended to be used by one or more persons and usually containing cooking, eating, living, sleeping and sanitary facilities.

label: Sentence
text: Hatchways to attic or roof spaces shall be fitted with doors or covers.

text: Masonry and Insulating Concrete Form Walls Not In Contact with the Ground

text: Application

text: General

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Article 9.20.1.2., this Section applies to

label: Clause
title: a)
text: unreinforced masonry and masonry veneer walls not in contact with the ground, where

title: i)
text: the height of the walls constructed on the foundation walls does not exceed 11 m, and

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: the roof or floor assembly above the first storey is not of concrete construction, and

references.link_text: First storey means the uppermost storey having its floor level not more than 2 m above grade .

label: Clause
title: b)
text: flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground that (see Note A-9.15.1.1.(1)(c) and 9.20.1.1.(1)(b))

title: i)

text: buildings not more than 2 storeys in building height , and

title: iii)
text: are erected in locations where the seismic spectral acceleration, S a (0.2), is not greater than 0.4 (see Note A-9.20.1.2.).

label: Sentence
text: For walls other than those described in Sentence (1), or where the masonry walls or insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground are designed for specified loads on the basis of ultimate and serviceability limit states, Subsection 4.3.2. shall apply.

label: Article
text: Earthquake Reinforcement

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.20.1.2.)

label: Sentence
text: In locations where the spectral acceleration, S a (0.2), is greater than 0.55, loadbearing elements of masonry buildings more than 1 storey in building height shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by Subsection 9.20.15.

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

Building height (in storeys ) means the number of storeys contained between the roof and the floor of the first storey .

label: Sentence
text: In locations where the spectral acceleration, S a (0.2), is greater than 0.35 but less than or equal to 0.55, loadbearing elements of masonry buildings 3 storeys in building height shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by Subsection 9.20.15.

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

text: Masonry Units

label: Article
text: Masonry Unit Standards

label: Sentence
text: Masonry units shall comply with

label: Clause
title: a)
text: ASTM C73, “Standard Specification for Calcium Silicate Brick (Sand-Lime Brick),”

label: Clause
title: b)
text: ASTM C126, “Ceramic Glazed Structural Clay Facing Tile, Facing Brick, and Solid Masonry Units,”

label: Clause
title: c)
text: ASTM C212, “Standard Specification for Structural Clay Facing Tile,”

label: Clause

label: Clause
title: f)
text: CSA A165.2, “Concrete brick masonry units,” or

label: Clause
title: g)
text: CSA A165.3, “Prefaced concrete masonry units.”

label: Article
text: Used Brick

label: Sentence
text: Used bricks shall be free of old mortar, soot or other surface coating and shall conform to Article 9.20.2.1.

label: Article
text: Glass Blocks

label: Sentence
text: Glass blocks shall not be used as loadbearing units or in the construction of fireplaces or chimneys .

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Article
text: Cellular Concrete

label: Sentence
text: Masonry made with cellular concrete shall not be used in contact with the soil or exposed to the weather.

references.link_text: Soil means that portion of the earth's crust that is fragmentary, or such that some individual particles of a dried sample may be readily separated by agitation in water; it includes boulders, cobbles, gravel, sand, silt, clay and organic matter.

label: Article
text: Stone

label: Sentence
text: Stone shall be sound and durable.

label: Article
text: Concrete Blocks Exposed to the Weather

label: Sentence
text: Concrete blocks exposed to the weather shall have density and water absorption characteristics conforming to concrete types A, B, C, or D described in CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units.”

text: Compressive Strength

label: Sentence
text: The compressive strength of concrete blocks shall conform to Table 9.20.2.7.

label: Subsection
text: Mortar

label: Article
text: Mortar Materials

label: Sentence
text: Cementitious materials and aggregates for mortar and grout shall comply with CAN/CSA-A179, “Mortar and Grout for Unit Masonry.”

label: Sentence
text: Water and aggregate shall be clean and free of significant amounts of deleterious materials.

label: Sentence
text: Lime used in mortar shall be hydrated.

label: Sentence
text: If lime putty is used in mortar, it shall be made by slaking quicklime in water for not less than 24 h or soaking hydrated lime in water for not less than 12 h.

label: Article
text: Mortar and Grout Mixes

label: Sentence
text: Mortar types shall be in accordance with Table 9.20.3.2.-A.

label: Sentence
text: Mortar for glass block masonry shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: Type S Portland cement-lime where exposed to the exterior, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: Type S or N where protected from the exterior.

label: Sentence
text: Mortar shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in Table 9.20.3.2.-B, with sufficient water to bring the mixture to a consistency adequate for laying masonry units.

label: Sentence
text: Grout shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in Table 9.20.3.2.-C, with sufficient water to provide a suitable flow to fill all voids completely, without excessive segregation or bleeding.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (6), mortar shall be used and placed in final position

label: Clause
title: a)
text: within 1.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is 25°C or higher, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: within 2.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is less than 25°C.

label: Sentence
text: Mortar and grout containing a set-control admixture shall be manufactured off-site in a batching plant and shall be used and placed in final position within a time not exceeding the useful life stipulated by the manufacturer.

label: Sentence
text: Grout used for reinforced masonry shall be placed in accordance with the requirements of CAN/CSA-A371, “Masonry Construction for Buildings.”

label: Subsection
text: Mortar Joints

label: Article
text: Thickness

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), mortar joint thickness for burned clay brick and concrete masonry units shall be 10 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Permitted tolerances in head and bed joints shall be not more than ± 5 mm.

label: Article
text: Masonry Units

label: Sentence
text: Hollow masonry units shall be laid with mortar applied to head and bed joints of both inner and outer face shells.

label: Sentence
text: Vertically aligned webs of hollow masonry units shall be laid in a full bed of mortar

label: Clause
title: a)
text: under the starting course,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: in all courses of columns, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: where adjacent to cells or cavities that are to be filled with grout.

label: Sentence
text: Except for head joints left open for weep holes and ventilation, solid masonry units shall be laid with full head and bed joints.

references.link_text: Solid masonry means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of solid masonry units or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. In multi-wythe masonry construction, the space between the wythes consists of a mortar-filled collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be constructed of the same masonry materials.

label: Subsection
text: Masonry Support

label: Article
text: Masonry Support

label: Sentence
text: All masonry shall be supported on masonry, concrete or steel, except that masonry veneer walls may be supported on foundations of wood frame constructed in conformance with Sentence 9.15.2.4.(1). (See Note A-9.20.5.1.(1).)

label: Sentence
text: Every masonry wall shall be at least as thick as the wall it supports, except as otherwise permitted in Article 9.20.12.2.

label: Article
text: Lintels or Arches

label: Sentence
text: Masonry over openings shall be supported by steel, masonry or reinforced concrete lintels, or masonry arches.

label: Sentence
text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry veneer above openings shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: conform to Table 9.20.5.2., and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: have a bearing length not less than 90 mm.

label: Table
title: Table 9.20.5.2.
text: Maximum Allowable Spans for Steel Lintels Supporting Masonry Veneer Forming Part of Sentence 9.20.5.2.(2) Minimum Angle Size, mm Maximum Allowable Spans, m Vertical Leg Horizontal Leg Thickness Supporting 75 mm Brick Supporting 90 mm Brick Supporting 100 mm Stone 89 76 6.4 2.55 — — 89 89 6.4 2.59 2.47 2.30 102 89 6.4 2.79 2.66 2.48 127 89 7.9 3.47 3.31 3.08 127 89 11 3.64 3.48 3.24

label: Sentence
text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry other than veneer, masonry and reinforced concrete lintels, and masonry arches shall be designed in accordance with Part 4 to support the imposed load.

label: Sentence
text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry shall be prime painted or otherwise protected from corrosion.

label: Subsection
text: Thickness and Height

label: Article
text: Thickness of Exterior Walls

label: Sentence
text: Masonry exterior walls, other than cavity walls , in 1- storey buildings and the top storeys of 2- and 3- storey buildings shall be not less than 140 mm thick, provided the walls are not more than 2.8 m high at the eaves and 4.6 m high at the peaks of gable ends.

label: Sentence
text: The exterior walls of the bottom storeys of 2- storey buildings , and exterior walls of the bottom 2 storeys of 3- storey buildings shall be not less than 190 mm thick.

label: Sentence
text: In exterior walls composed of more than one wythe, each wythe shall be not less than 90 mm thick.

label: Article
text: Cavity Walls

label: Sentence
text: Cavity walls shall be made with not less than 90 mm wide units if the joints are raked and not less than 75 mm wide units if the joints are not raked.

label: Sentence
text: The width of a cavity in a cavity wall shall be not less than 50 mm and not greater than 150 mm.

references.link_text: Cavity wall means a construction of masonry units laid with a cavity between the wythes. The wythes are tied together with metal ties or bonding units, and are relied on to act together in resisting lateral loads.

label: Sentence
text: The minimum thickness of cavity walls above the supporting base shall be 230 mm for the top 7.6 m and 330 mm for the remaining portion, except that where 75 mm wide units are used, the wall height above the top of the foundation wall shall not exceed 6 m.

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

label: Article
text: Thickness of Interior Walls

label: Sentence
text: The thickness of loadbearing interior walls shall be determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3).

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Sentence
text: The thickness of interior non- loadbearing walls shall be

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Clause
title: a)
text: determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3), and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: in any case, not less than 65 mm.

label: Article
text: Masonry Veneer

label: Sentence
text: Except for masonry veneer where each masonry unit is supported individually by the structural backing, masonry veneer shall consist of solid masonry units not less than 75 mm thick.

label: Sentence
text: Veneer described in Sentence (1) over wood-frame walls shall have not less than a 25 mm air space behind the veneer.

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer less than 90 mm thick shall have unraked joints.

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer shall conform to Subsection 4.3.2., where the masonry units are required to be individually supported by the structural backing.

label: Article
text: Parapet Walls

label: Sentence
text: The height of parapet walls above the adjacent roof surface shall be not more than 3 times the parapet wall thickness.

label: Sentence
text: Parapet walls shall be solid masonry

references.link_text: Solid masonry means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of solid masonry units or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. In multi-wythe masonry construction, the space between the wythes consists of a mortar-filled collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be constructed of the same masonry materials.

label: Clause
title: a)
text: with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar, grout, or concrete, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: that extends from the top of the parapet to not less than 300 mm below the adjacent roof level.

label: Article
text: Stone or Concrete Facings

label: Sentence
text: Slab and panel facings of precast concrete and natural or artificial stone shall conform to Subsection 4.3.2.

label: Subsection
text: Chases and Recesses

label: Article
text: Maximum Dimensions

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence 9.20.7.2.(2) and Article 9.20.7.4., the depth of any chase or recess shall not exceed one third the thickness of the wall, and the width of the chase or recess shall not exceed 500 mm.

label: Article
text: Minimum Wall Thickness

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2) and Article 9.20.7.4., no chase or recess shall be constructed in any wall 190 mm or less in thickness.

label: Sentence
text: Recesses may be constructed in 190 mm walls provided they do not exceed 100 mm in depth, 750 mm in height and 500 mm in width.

label: Article
text: Separation of Chases or Recesses

label: Sentence
text: Chases and recesses shall be not less than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 4 times the wall thickness apart, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 600 mm away from any pilaster, cross wall, buttress or other vertical element providing required lateral support for the wall.

label: Article
text: Non-Conforming Chases or Recesses

label: Sentence
text: Chases or recesses that do not conform to the limits specified in Articles 9.20.7.1. to 9.20.7.3. shall be considered as openings, and any masonry supported above such a chase or recess shall be supported by a lintel or arch as provided in Article 9.20.5.2.

label: Article
text: Chases or Recesses Cut into Walls

label: Sentence
text: Chases and recesses shall not be cut into walls made with hollow units after the masonry units are in place.

label: Subsection
text: Support of Loads

label: Article
text: Capping of Hollow Masonry Walls

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), loadbearing walls of hollow masonry units supporting roof or floor framing members shall be capped with not less than 50 mm of solid masonry or have the top course filled with concrete.

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

Solid masonry means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of solid masonry units or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. In multi-wythe masonry construction, the space between the wythes consists of a mortar-filled collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be constructed of the same masonry materials.

label: Sentence
text: Capping required in Sentence (1) may be omitted where the roof framing is supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm by 89 mm.

label: Article
text: Cavity Walls Supporting Framing Members

label: Sentence
text: Floor joists supported on cavity walls shall be supported on solid masonry units not less than 57 mm high.

label: Sentence
text: Floor joists described in Sentence (1) shall not project into the cavity.

label: Sentence
text: Roof and ceiling framing members bearing on cavity walls shall be supported on

label: Clause
title: a)
text: solid masonry units not less than 57 mm high that bridge the full thickness of the wall, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: a wood plate not less than 38 mm thick, bearing not less than 50 mm on each wythe.

label: Article
text: Bearing of Beams and Joists

label: Sentence
text: The bearing area under beams and joists shall be sufficient to carry the supported load.

label: Sentence
text: In no case shall the minimum length of end bearing of beams supported on masonry be less than 90 mm.

label: Sentence
text: The length of end bearing of floor, roof or ceiling joists supported on masonry shall be not less than 40 mm.

label: Article
text: Support of Beams and Columns

label: Sentence
text: Beams and columns supported on masonry walls shall be supported on pilasters where the thickness of the masonry wall or wythe is less than 190 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Not less than 190 mm depth of solid masonry or concrete shall be provided under the beam or column referred to in Sentence (1).

references.link_text: Solid masonry means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of solid masonry units or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. In multi-wythe masonry construction, the space between the wythes consists of a mortar-filled collar joint or grout-filled space and the wythes may or may not be constructed of the same masonry materials.

label: Sentence
text: Pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be bonded or tied to masonry walls.

label: Sentence
text: Concrete pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 50 mm by 300 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Unit masonry pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 100 mm by 290 mm.

label: Article
text: Projection of Masonry Veneer Beyond Supporting Members

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer of solid masonry units resting on a bearing support shall not project more than one third of the thickness of the veneer. (See Note A-9.20.8.5.(1).)

label: Sentence
text: Where the masonry veneer described in Sentence (1) is rough stone masonry,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the projection shall be measured as the average projection of the units, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the thickness of the veneer shall be measured as the average thickness of the veneer.

label: Subsection
text: Bonding and Tying

label: Article
text: Joints to be Offset or Reinforced

label: Sentence
text: Vertical joints in adjacent masonry courses shall be offset unless each wythe of masonry is reinforced with the equivalent of not less than 2 corrosion-resistant steel bars of 3.76 mm diam placed in the horizontal joints at vertical intervals not exceeding 460 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Where joints in the reinforcing referred to in Sentence (1) occur, the bars shall be lapped not less than 150 mm.

label: Article
text: Bonding or Tying of Other than Masonry Veneer

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Article 9.20.9.5. regarding masonry veneer, masonry walls that consist of 2 or more wythes shall have the wythes bonded or tied together with masonry bonding units as described in Article 9.20.9.3. or with metal ties as described in Article 9.20.9.4.

label: Article
text: Bonding

label: Sentence
text: Where wythes are bonded together with masonry units, the bonding units shall comprise not less than 4% of the wall surface area.

label: Sentence
text: Bonding units described in Sentence (1) shall be spaced not more than 600 mm vertically and horizontally in the case of brick masonry and 900 mm o.c. in the case of block or tile.

label: Sentence
text: Units described in Sentence (1) shall extend not less than 90 mm into adjacent wythes.

label: Article
text: Tying

label: Sentence
text: Where 2 or more wythes are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the ties shall conform to the requirements in Sentences (3) to (6).

label: Sentence
text: Other ties may be used where it can be shown that such ties provide walls that are at least as strong and as durable as those made with the individual rod type.

label: Sentence
text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: be corrosion-resistant,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: have a minimum cross-sectional area of not less than 17.8 mm 2 , and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: have not less than a 50 mm portion bent at right angles at each end.

label: Sentence
text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: extend from within 25 mm of the outer face of the wall to within 25 mm of the inner face of the wall,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: be completely embedded in mortar except for the portion exposed in cavity walls , and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: be staggered from course to course.

label: Sentence
text: Where 2 or more wythes in walls other than cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the space between wythes shall be completely filled with mortar.

label: Sentence
text: Ties described in Sentence (5) shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: located within 300 mm of openings and spaced not more than 900 mm apart around openings, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 460 mm apart vertically at other locations.

label: Sentence
text: Except as required in Sentences (8) and (9), where the inner and outer wythes of cavity walls are tied with individual wire ties, the ties shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 400 mm apart vertically.

label: Sentence
text: Within 100 mm of the bottom of each floor or roof assembly where the cavity extends below the assemblies, the ties described in Sentence (7) shall be spaced not more than 600 mm apart horizontally.

label: Sentence
text: Within 300 mm of any openings, the ties described in Sentence (7) shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart.

label: Article
text: Ties for Masonry Veneer

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer 75 mm or more in thickness and resting on a bearing support shall be tied to masonry backing or to wood framing members with straps that are

label: Clause
title: a)
text: corrosion-resistant,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: not less than 0.76 mm thick,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: not less than 22 mm wide,

label: Clause
title: d)
text: shaped to provide a key with the mortar,

label: Clause
title: e)
text: pre-bent during manufacture to a right angle within 6 mm of the fastener hole,

label: Clause
title: f)
text: fastened with

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: corrosion-resistant wood screws conforming to Sentence 9.23.3.1.(3) that have a minimum diameter of 4.16 mm (No. 8) and a wood penetration of not less than 38 mm, or

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: corrosion-resistant common spiral nails conforming to Sentence 9.23.3.1.(1) that are not less than 76 mm long and have a wood penetration of not less than 63 mm, and

label: Clause
title: g)
text: spaced in accordance with Table 9.20.9.5.

label: Sentence
text: Where hot-dipped, zinc-coated straps are used to meet the requirements of Sentence (1), they shall be pre-bent and pre-drilled or pre-punched prior to hot-dip, zinc-coated galvanizing.

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer individually supported by masonry or wood-frame backing shall be secured to the backing in conformance with Subsection 4.3.2.

label: Article
text: Reinforcing for Glass Block

label: Sentence
text: Glass block shall have horizontal joint reinforcement of 2 corrosion-resistant bars of not less than 3.76 mm diam or expanded metal strips not less than 75 mm wide

label: Clause
title: a)
text: spaced at vertical intervals of not more than 600 mm for units 200 mm or less in height, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: installed in every horizontal joint for units higher than 200 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Reinforcement required in Sentence (1) shall be lapped not less than 150 mm.

label: Subsection
text: Lateral Support

label: Article
text: Lateral Support Required

label: Sentence
text: Masonry walls shall be laterally supported by floor or roof construction or by intersecting masonry walls or buttresses.

label: Sentence
text: The spacing of supports required in Sentence (1) shall be not more than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 20 times the wall thickness for all loadbearing walls and exterior non- loadbearing walls, and

title: b)

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Sentence
