text: two-thirds of the sum of the thicknesses of the wythes, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the thickness of the thicker wythe.

label: Sentence
text: Floor and roof constructions providing lateral support for walls as required in Sentence (1) shall be constructed to transfer lateral loads to walls or buttresses approximately at right angles to the laterally supported walls.

label: Subsection
text: Anchorage of Roofs, Floors and Intersecting Walls

label: Article
text: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require Lateral Support

label: Sentence
text: Where required to receive lateral support (see Subsection 9.20.10.), masonry walls shall be anchored to each floor or roof assembly at maximum intervals of 2 m, except that anchorage to floor joists not more than 1 m above grade may be omitted.

references.link_text: Grade means the lowest of the average levels of finished ground adjoining each exterior wall of a building , except that localized depressions need not be considered in the determination of average levels of finished ground. (See First storey and Note A-1.4.1.2.(1).) Groundwater means a free standing body of water in the ground.

label: Sentence
text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be corrosion-resistant and be not less than the equivalent of 40 mm by 4.76 mm thick steel straps.

label: Sentence
text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be shaped to provide a mechanical key with the masonry and shall be securely fastened to the horizontal support to develop the full strength of the anchor.

label: Sentence
text: When joists are parallel to the wall, anchors required in Sentence (1) shall extend across not less than 3 joists.

label: Article
text: Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require Lateral Support

label: Sentence
text: Where required to provide lateral support, intersecting walls shall be bonded or tied together.

label: Sentence
text: Where bonding is used to satisfy the requirements of Sentence (1), 50% of the adjacent masonry units in the intersecting wall, distributed uniformly over the height of the intersection, shall be embedded in the laterally supported wall.

label: Sentence
text: Where tying is used to satisfy the requirements of Sentence (1), the ties shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: corrosion-resistant metal,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: equivalent to not less than 4.76 mm by 40 mm steel strapping,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: spaced not more than 800 mm o.c. vertically, and

label: Clause
title: d)
text: shaped at both ends to provide sufficient mechanical key to develop the strength of the ties.

label: Article
text: Anchoring Intersecting Wood-Frame Walls to Masonry Walls

label: Sentence
text: Wood-frame walls shall be anchored to masonry walls that they intersect with not less than 4.76 mm diam corrosion-resistant steel rods spaced not more than 900 mm o.c. vertically.

label: Sentence
text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be fastened to the wood framing at one end and shaped to provide a mechanical key at the other end to develop the strength of the anchor.

label: Article
text: Anchoring Wood-Frame Roof Systems to Masonry Walls

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), roof systems of wood-frame construction shall be anchored to exterior masonry walls by not less than 12.7 mm diam anchor bolts,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: spaced not more than 2.4 m apart,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: embedded not less than 90 mm into the masonry, and

label: Clause
title: c)
text: fastened to a rafter plate of not less than 38 mm thick lumber.

label: Sentence
text: The roof system described in Sentence (1) is permitted to be anchored by nailing the wall furring strips to the side of the rafter plate.

label: Article
text: Anchoring Masonry Cornices, Sills and Trim to Masonry Walls

label: Sentence
text: Cornices, sills or other trim of masonry material which project beyond the wall face shall have not less than 65% of their mass, but not less than 90 mm, within the wall or shall be adequately anchored to the wall with corrosion-resistant anchors.

label: Article
text: Anchoring to Masonry Piers

label: Sentence
text: Where anchor bolts are to be placed in the top of a masonry pier, the pier shall conform to the requirements of Sentence 9.15.2.3.(4) and shall be capped with concrete or reinforced masonry not less than 200 mm thick.

label: Subsection
text: Corbelling

label: Article
text: Corbelling

label: Sentence
text: All corbelling shall consist of solid masonry units .

label: Sentence
text: The units referred to in Sentence (1) shall be corbelled so that the horizontal projection of any unit does not exceed 25 mm and the total projection does not exceed one third of the total wall thickness.

label: Article
text: Corbelling for Cavity Walls

label: Sentence
text: Cavity walls of greater thickness than the foundation wall on which they rest shall not be corbelled but may project 25 mm over the outer face of the foundation wall disregarding parging.

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .
Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

text: the projection of each course does not exceed half the height or one third the thickness of the corbelled unit, and

title: b)

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

label: Article
text: Corbelling for Masonry Veneer

label: Sentence
text: Masonry veneer resting on a bearing support shall not project more than 25 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is not less than 90 mm thick, and 12 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is less than 90 mm thick.

label: Sentence
text: In the case of rough stone veneer, the projection, measured as the average projection of the stone units, shall not exceed one-third the bed width beyond the supporting base.

text: Protection of Interior Finish

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), where the interior finish of the exterior walls of a building is a type that may be damaged by moisture, exterior masonry walls, other than cavity walls or walls that are protected for their full height by a roof of a carport or porch, shall be covered on the interior surface with sheathing membrane conforming to CAN/CGSB-51.32-M, “Sheathing, Membrane, Breather Type,” lapped not less than 100 mm at the joints.

text: In situations described in Sentence (1), flashing shall be provided where water will accumulate, to lead it to the exterior.

text: Mortar Droppings

label: Sentence
text: Cavity walls shall be constructed so that mortar droppings are prevented from forming a bridge to allow the passage of rain water across the cavity.

label: Article

label: Sentence
text: The junction of door and window frames with masonry shall be caulked in conformance with Subsection 9.27.4.

label: Article
text: Drips beneath Window Sills

label: Sentence
text: Where no flashing is installed beneath window sills, such sills shall be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the wall surface.

text: Protection during Work

label: Article
text: Laying Temperature of Mortar and Masonry

label: Sentence
text: Mortar and masonry shall be maintained at a temperature not below 5°C during installation and for not less than 48 h after installation.

label: Sentence
text: No frozen material shall be used in mortar mix.

label: Article
text: Protection from Weather

label: Sentence
text: The top surface of uncompleted masonry exposed to the weather shall be completely covered with a waterproofing material when construction is not in progress.

text: Amount of Reinforcement

text: Where reinforcement is required in this Section, masonry walls shall be reinforced horizontally and vertically with steel having a total cross-sectional area of not less than 0.002 times the horizontal cross-sectional area of the wall, so that not less than one-third of the required steel area is installed either horizontally or vertically and the remainder in the other direction.

label: Article
text: Installation Standard

label: Sentence
text: Where reinforcement for masonry is required in this Section, it shall be installed in conformance with the requirements for reinforced masonry as contained in CAN/CSA-A371, “Masonry Construction for Buildings.”

label: Sentence

label: Article
text: Chimney or Flue Pipe Walls

label: Sentence
text: The walls of any chimney or flue pipe shall be constructed so as to be smoke- and flame-tight.

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Subsection
text: Chimney Flues

label: Article
text: Chimney Flue Limitations

label: Sentence
text: A chimney flue that serves a fireplace or incinerator shall not serve any other appliance .

label: Sentence
text: A chimney flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall not be connected to a natural-gas- or propane-fired appliance .

label: Sentence
text: A chimney flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall not be connected to an oil-burning appliance unless the solid-fuel-burning appliance is certified for such installation and the installation of both appliances meets the requirements of the relevant standards referenced in Article 9.33.5.2.

label: Article
text: Connections of More Than One Appliance

label: Sentence
text: Except as required by Article 9.21.2.1., where two or more fuel-burning appliances are connected to the same chimney flue , the connections shall be made as described in Sentences (2) to (4) and an adequate draft shall be provided for the connected appliances in conformance with the requirements of the relevant standards listed in Subsection 9.33.10.

label: Sentence
text: Where 2 or more fuel-burning appliances are connected to the same chimney flue , the appliances shall be located on the same storey .

references.link_text: Storey means that portion of a building that is situated between the top of any floor and the top of the floor next above it, and if there is no floor above it, that portion between the top of such floor and the ceiling above it.

label: Sentence
text: The connection referred to in Sentence (2) for a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall be made below connections for appliances burning other fuels.

label: Sentence
text: The connection referred to in Sentence (2) for a liquid-fuel-burning appliance shall be made below any connections for appliances burning natural gas or propane.

label: Article
text: Inclined Chimney Flues

label: Sentence
text: Chimney flues shall not be inclined more than 45° to the vertical.

label: Article
text: Size of Chimney Flues

label: Sentence
text: Except for chimneys serving fireplaces, the size of a chimney flue shall conform to the requirements of the appliance installation standards referenced in Sentences 9.33.5.2.(1) and 9.33.5.3.(1).

label: Sentence
text: Where a chimney flue serves only one appliance , the flue area shall be at least equal to that of the flue pipe connected to it.

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.
Flue pipe means the pipe connecting the flue collar of an appliance to a chimney .

label: Article
text: Fireplace Chimneys

label: Sentence
text: The size of a chimney flue serving a masonry fireplace shall conform to

label: Article
text: Oval Chimney Flues

label: Sentence
text: The width of an oval chimney flue shall be not less than two-thirds its breadth.

label: Subsection
text: Chimney Lining

label: Article
text: Lining Materials

label: Sentence
text: Every masonry or concrete chimney shall have a lining of clay, concrete, firebrick or metal.

label: Article
text: Joints in Chimney Liners

label: Sentence
text: Joints of chimney liners shall be sealed to provide a barrier to the passage of flue gases and condensate into the cavity between the liner and the surrounding masonry.

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.

label: Sentence
text: Joints of clay, concrete or firebrick chimney liners shall be struck flush to provide a straight, smooth, aligned chimney flue .

label: Article
text: Clay Liners

label: Sentence
text: Clay liners shall conform to CAN/CSA-A324-M, “Clay Flue Liners.”

label: Sentence
text: Liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 15.9 mm thick and shall be capable of resisting, without softening or cracking, a temperature of 1 100°C.

label: Article
text: Firebrick Liners

label: Sentence
text: Firebrick liners shall conform to ASTM C27, “Standard Classification of Fireclay and High-Alumina Refractory Brick.”

label: Sentence
text: Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar.”

label: Article
text: Concrete Liners

label: Sentence
text: Concrete flue liners shall conform to Clause 4.2.6.4 of CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces.”

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.

label: Article
text: Metal Liners

label: Sentence
text: Metal liners shall be constructed of not less than 0.3 mm thick stainless steel.

label: Sentence
text: Metal liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall only be used in chimneys serving gas- or oil-burning appliances . (See Note A-9.21.3.6.(2).)

label: Article
text: Installation of Chimney Liners

label: Sentence
text: Chimney liners shall be installed when the surrounding masonry or concrete is placed.

label: Article
text: Spaces between Liners and Surrounding Masonry

label: Sentence
text: A space not less than 10 mm wide shall be left between a chimney liner and surrounding masonry.

references.link_text: Chimney liner means a conduit containing a chimney flue used as a lining of a masonry or concrete chimney .

label: Sentence
text: The space required in Sentence (1) shall not be filled with mortar.

label: Article
text: Mortar for Chimney Liners

label: Sentence
text: Chimney liners used in chimneys for solid-fuel-burning appliances shall be laid in a full bed of

label: Clause
title: a)
text: high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar,” or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

label: Sentence
text: Chimney liners used in chimneys for oil- or gas-burning appliances shall be laid in a full bed of mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

label: Article
text: Extension of Chimney Liners

label: Sentence
text: Chimney liners shall extend from a point not less than 200 mm below the lowest flue pipe connection to a point not less than 50 mm or more than 100 mm above the chimney cap.

text: Footings for masonry chimneys and concrete chimneys shall conform to

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Article
text: Chimney Caps

label: Sentence
text: The top of a chimney shall have a waterproof cap of reinforced concrete, masonry or metal.

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Sentence
text: The cap required in Sentence (1) shall slope from the lining and be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the chimney wall.

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Sentence
text: Cast-in-place concrete caps shall be separated from the chimney liner by a bond break and be sealed at that location.

references.link_text: Chimney liner means a conduit containing a chimney flue used as a lining of a masonry or concrete chimney .

text: Jointed precast concrete or masonry chimney caps shall have flashing installed beneath the cap extending from the liner to the drip edge.

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Article
text: Cleanout

label: Sentence
text: A cleanout opening with a metal frame and a tight-fitting metal door shall be installed near the base of the chimney flue .

text: The walls of a masonry chimney shall be built of solid masonry units not less than 75 mm thick.

references.link_text: Chimney means a primarily vertical shaft enclosing at least one flue for conducting flue gases to the outdoors.

label: Article
text: Separation of Flue Liners

label: Sentence
text: Flue liners in the same chimney shall be separated by not less than 75 mm of masonry or concrete exclusive of liners where clay liners are used, or 90 mm of firebrick where firebrick liners are used.

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.

label: Sentence
text: Flue liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall be installed to prevent significant lateral movement.

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.

label: Article
text: Flashing

label: Sentence
text: Junctions with adjacent materials shall be adequately flashed to shed water.

text: Combustible flooring and subflooring shall have not less than a 12 mm clearance from masonry or concrete chimneys .

label: Article
text: Sealing of Spaces

text: All spaces between masonry or concrete chimneys and combustible framing shall be sealed top or bottom with noncombustible material.

Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Article

text: Joists or beams may be supported on masonry walls which enclose chimney flues provided the combustible members are separated from the flue by not less than 290 mm of solid masonry .

Solid masonry means a single wythe or multi-wythe construction made of solid masonry units or semi-solid, cored, or hollow masonry units, the cells of which may or may not be filled with mortar or grout. label: Section
title: Section 9.22.
text: Fireplaces

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Application

label: Sentence
text: Except when otherwise specifically stated herein, this Section applies to masonry fireplaces constructed on-site.

label: Article
text: Masonry and Concrete

label: Sentence
text: Except as otherwise stated in this Section, unit masonry shall conform to

label: Sentence
text: Masonry above openings shall be supported by steel lintels conforming to Sentence 9.20.5.2.(2), reinforced concrete or a masonry arch.

label: Article
text: Footings

label: Sentence
text: Footings for masonry and concrete fireplaces shall conform to Section 9.15.

label: Article
text: Combustion Air

label: Sentence
text: Where a supply of combustion air is provided directly to the fire chamber of a fireplace, including a factory-built fireplace, the installation shall comply with the “Outdoor Air Supply” requirements provided in CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces.”

label: Subsection
text: Fireplace Liners

label: Article
text: Brick or Steel Liners

label: Sentence
text: Except where a fireplace is equipped with a steel liner, every fireplace shall have a firebrick liner.

label: Article
text: Firebrick Liners

label: Sentence
text: Firebrick liners shall be not less than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 50 mm thick for the sides and back, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 25 mm thick for the floor.

label: Sentence
text: Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar.”

label: Sentence
text: Joints between a firebrick liner and the adjacent backing masonry shall be offset.

label: Article
text: Steel Liners

label: Sentence
text: Steel liners for fireplaces shall conform to CAN/ULC-S639-M, “Standard for Steel Liner Assemblies for Solid-Fuel Burning Masonry Fireplaces,” and shall be installed in accordance with the installation instructions in that standard.

label: Subsection
text: Fireplace Walls

label: Article
text: Thickness of Walls

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), the thickness of the back and sides of a fireplace, including the thickness of any firebrick liner, shall be not less than 190 mm where a metal liner or a firebrick liner less than 51 mm thick is used.

label: Sentence
text: When a steel fireplace liner is used with an air circulating chamber surrounding the firebox, the back and sides of the fireplace shall consist of

label: Clause
title: a)
text: solid masonry units not less than 90 mm thick, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: hollow masonry units not less than 190 mm thick.

label: Subsection
text: Fire Chamber

label: Article
text: Fire Chamber Dimensions

label: Sentence
text: The distance from the back of the fire chamber to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be not less than 300 mm.

label: Subsection
text: Hearth

label: Article
text: Hearth Extension

label: Sentence
text: Except as required in Sentence (2), fireplaces shall have a noncombustible hearth extending not less than 400 mm in front of the fireplace opening and not less than 200 mm beyond each side of the fireplace opening.

references.link_text: Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Sentence
text: Where the fire chamber floor is elevated more than 150 mm above the hearth, the dimension of the hearth measured perpendicular to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be increased by not less than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 50 mm for an elevation above 150 mm and not more than 300 mm, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: an additional 25 mm for every 50 mm in elevation above 300 mm.

label: Article
text: Support of Hearth

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), the fire chamber floor and hearth shall be supported on a reinforced concrete slab not less than 100 mm thick at its supports and, if cantilevered, not less than 50 mm thick at its unsupported edge.

label: Sentence
text: A hearth for a fireplace with an opening raised not less than 200 mm from a combustible floor is permitted to be supported on that floor provided the requirements of Clauses 5.3.6.5. to 5.3.6.7. of CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces,” are followed.

references.link_text: Combustible means that a material fails to meet the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Combustible construction means that type of construction that does not meet the requirements for noncombustible construction or encapsulated mass timber construction .

label: Subsection
text: Damper

label: Article
text: Required Damper and Size

label: Sentence
text: The throat of every fireplace shall be equipped with a metal damper sufficiently large to cover the full area of the throat opening.

label: Subsection
text: Smoke Chamber

label: Article
text: Slope of Smoke Chamber

label: Sentence
text: The sides of the smoke chamber connecting a fireplace throat with a flue shall not be sloped at an angle greater than 45° to the vertical.

references.link_text: Flue means an enclosed passageway for conveying flue gases.

label: Article
text: Wall Thickness

label: Sentence
text: The thickness of masonry walls surrounding the smoke chamber shall be not less than 190 mm at the sides, front and back, except that the portions of the back exposed to the outside may be 140 mm thick.

label: Subsection
text: Factory-Built Fireplaces

label: Article
text: Conformance to Standard

label: Sentence
text: Factory-built fireplaces and their installation shall conform to CAN/ULC-S610, “Standard for Factory-Built Fireplace Systems.”

label: Subsection
text: Clearance of Combustible Material

label: Sentence

label: Subsection
text: Fireplace Inserts and Hearth-Mounted Stoves

label: Article
text: Appliance Standard

label: Sentence
text: Fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to ULC-S628, “Standard for Fireplace Inserts.”

label: Article
text: Installation

label: Sentence
text: The installation of fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to CSA B365, “Installation Code for Solid-Fuel-Burning Appliances and Equipment.”

label: Section
title: Section 9.23.
text: Wood-Frame Construction

label: Subsection
text: Application

label: Article
text: Limitations

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.23.1.1.)

label: Sentence
text: This Section applies to constructions where wall, floor and roof planes are generally comprised of lumber frames of small repetitive structural members, or engineered components, and where

label: Clause
title: a)
text: roof and wall planes are clad, sheathed or braced on at least one side,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the small repetitive structural members are spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: the constructions do not serve as foundations ,

label: Clause
title: d)
text: the specified live load on supported subfloors and floor framing does not exceed 2.4 kPa, and

label: Clause
title: e)
text: the span of any structural member does not exceed 12.20 m.

label: Sentence
text: Where the conditions in Sentence (1) are exceeded for wood constructions, the design of the framing and fastening shall conform to Subsection 4.3.1.

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Strength and Rigidity

label: Sentence
text: All members shall be so framed, anchored, fastened, tied and braced to provide the necessary strength and rigidity.

label: Article
text: Protection from Decay

label: Sentence
text: Ends of wood joists, beams and other members framing into masonry or concrete shall be treated to prevent decay where the bottom of the member is at or below ground level, or a 12 mm air space shall be provided at the end and sides of the member.

label: Sentence
text: Air spaces required in Sentence (1) shall not be blocked by insulation, vapour barriers or airtight materials.

label: Article
text: Protection from Dampness

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), wood framing members that are not pressure-treated with a wood preservative and that are supported on concrete in contact with the ground or fill shall be separated from the concrete by not less than 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.

label: Sentence
text: Dampproofing material referred to in Sentence (1) is not required where the wood member is at least 150 mm above the ground.

label: Article
text: Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), connectors in contact with preservative-treated wood shall be made of

title: a)
text: hot-dipped, zinc-coated galvanized steel with a coating weight not less than Z550 conforming to ASTM A653/A653M, “Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, Zinc-Coated (Galvanized) or Zinc-Iron Alloy-Coated (Galvannealed) by the Hot-Dip Process,”

label: Clause
title: b)
text: a material that provides an equivalent level of corrosion protection to that provided by the material described in Clause (a), or

label: Clause
title: c)
text: stainless steel.

label: Sentence
text: Fasteners used to attach the connectors referred to in Sentence (1) shall be made of

label: Clause
title: a)
text: galvanized steel coated with zinc in accordance with ASTM A153/A153M, “Standard Specification for Zinc Coating (Hot-Dip) on Iron and Steel Hardware,” or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: a material that provides an equivalent level of performance and is compatible with the connector.

label: Sentence
text: Connectors and fasteners that are in contact with wood that has been treated with a disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (SBX (DOT)) or zinc borate preservative and is installed in a dry interior environment are permitted to be made of uncoated carbon steel. (See Note A-9.23.2.4.(3).)

text: Application

label: Sentence
text: Spans provided in this Subsection for joists, beams and lintels supporting floors shall apply only where

references.link_text: Live load means a variable load due to the intended use and occupancy that is to be assumed in the design of the structural members of a building . It includes loads due to cranes and the pressure of liquids in containers.

label: Sentence
text: Spans for floor joists that are not selected from Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A and 9.23.4.2.-B and that are required to be designed for the same loading conditions, shall not exceed the design requirements for uniform loading and vibration criteria.

label: Sentence
text: Spans for built-up wood and glued-laminated timber floor beams shall conform to the spans in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-H to 9.23.4.2.-K. (See Article 9.4.2.2.)

label: Sentence
text: Spans for roof ridge beams shall conform to the spans in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-L for the uniform snow load shown. (See Articles 9.4.2.2. and 9.23.14.8.)

label: Subsection
text: Notching and Drilling

label: Article
text: Holes Drilled in Framing Members

label: Sentence
text: Holes drilled in roof, floor or ceiling framing members shall be not larger than one-quarter the depth of the member and shall be located not less than 50 mm from the edges, unless the depth of the member is increased by the size of the hole.

label: Article
text: Notching of Framing Members

label: Sentence
text: Floor, roof and ceiling framing members are permitted to be notched provided the notch is located on the top of the member within half the joist depth from the edge of bearing and is not deeper than one-third the joist depth, unless the depth of the member is increased by the size of the notch.

label: Article
text: Wall Studs

label: Sentence
text: Wall studs shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise damaged so that the undamaged portion of the stud is less than two-thirds the depth of the stud if the stud is loadbearing or 40 mm if the stud is non- loadbearing , unless the weakened studs are suitably reinforced.

references.link_text: Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

Loadbearing (as applying to a building element) means subjected to or designed to carry loads in addition to its own dead load , excepting a wall element subjected only to wind or earthquake loads in addition to its own dead load .

label: Article
text: Top Plates

label: Sentence
text: Top plates in walls shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise weakened to reduce the undamaged width to less than 50 mm unless the weakened plates are suitably reinforced.

label: Article
text: Roof Trusses

label: Sentence
text: Roof truss members shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise weakened unless such notching or drilling is allowed for in the design of the truss.

text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3), exterior columns and posts shall be anchored to resist uplift and lateral movement.

label: Subsection
text: Beams to Support Floors

label: Article
text: Bearing for Beams

label: Sentence
text: Beams shall have even and level bearing and the bearing at end supports shall be not less than 89 mm long, except as stated in the notes to Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-H to 9.23.4.2.-K.

label: Article
text: Priming of Steel Beams

label: Sentence
text: Exterior steel beams shall be shop primed.

label: Article
text: Built-up Wood Beams

label: SeeAlso
text: (See Note A-9.23.8.3.)

label: Sentence
text: Where a beam is made up of individual pieces of lumber that are nailed together, the individual members shall be 38 mm or greater in thickness and installed on edge.

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (3), where individual members of a built-up beam are butted together to form a joint, the joint shall occur over a support.

label: Sentence
text: Where a beam is continuous over more than one span, individual members are permitted to be butted together to form a joint at or within 150 mm of the end quarter points of the clear spans, provided the quarter points are not those closest to the ends of the beam.

label: Sentence
text: Members joined at quarter points shall be continuous over adjacent supports.

label: Sentence
text: Joints in individual members of a beam that are located at or near the end quarter points shall not occur in adjacent members at the same quarter point and shall not reduce the effective beam width by more than half.

label: Sentence
text: Not more than one butt joint shall occur in any individual member of a built-up beam within any one span.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (8), where 38 mm members are laid on edge to form a built-up beam, individual members shall be nailed together with a double row of nails not less than 89 mm in length, spaced not more than 450 mm apart in each row with the end nails located 100 mm to 150 mm from the end of each piece.

label: Sentence
text: Where 38 mm members in built-up wood beams are not nailed together as provided in Sentence (7), they shall be bolted together with not less than 12.7 mm diam bolts equipped with washers and spaced not more than 1.2 m o.c., with the end bolts located not more than 600 mm from the ends of the members.

label: Subsection
text: Floor Joists

label: Article
text: End Bearing for Joists

label: Sentence
text: Except when supported on ribbon boards, floor joists shall have not less than 38 mm length of end bearing.

label: Sentence
text: Ribbon boards referred to in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 19 mm by 89 mm lumber let into the studs.

label: Article
text: Joists Supported by Beams

label: Sentence
text: Floor joists may be supported on the tops of beams or may be framed into the sides of beams.

label: Sentence
text: When framed into the side of a wood beam, joists referred to in Sentence (1) shall be supported on

label: Clause
title: a)
text: joist hangers or other acceptable mechanical connectors, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: not less than 38 mm by 64 mm ledger strips nailed to the side of the beam, except that 38 mm by 38 mm ledger strips may be used provided each joist is nailed to the beam by not less than four 89 mm nails, in addition to the nailing for the ledger strip required in Table 9.23.3.4.

label: Sentence
text: When framed into the side of a steel beam, joists referred to in Sentence (1) shall be supported on the bottom flange of the beam or on not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber bolted to the web with not less than 6.3 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 600 mm apart.

label: Sentence
text: Joists referred to in Sentence (3) shall be spliced above the beam with not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber at least 600 mm long to support the flooring.

label: Sentence
text: Not less than a 12 mm space shall be provided between the splice required in Sentence (4) and the beam to allow for shrinkage of the wood joists.

label: Article
text: Restraint of Joist Bottoms

label: Sentence

text: Header Joists

label: Sentence

label: Sentence

label: Sentence

text: Support of Tail and Header Joists

label: Sentence

label: Subsection
text: Roof and Ceiling Framing

label: Article
text: Continuity of Rafters and Joists

label: Sentence
text: Roof rafters and joists and ceiling joists shall be continuous or shall be spliced over vertical supports that extend to suitable bearing.

label: Article
text: Framing around Openings

label: Sentence
text: Roof and ceiling framing members shall be doubled on each side of openings greater than 2 rafter or joist spacings wide.

label: Article
text: End Bearing Length

label: Sentence
text: The length of end bearing of joists and rafters shall be not less than 38 mm.

label: Article
text: Location and Attachment of Rafters

label: Sentence
text: Rafters shall be located directly opposite each other and tied together at the peak, or may be offset by their own thickness if nailed to a ridge board not less than 17.5 mm thick.

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (3), framing members shall be connected by gusset plates or nailing at the peak in conformance with Table 9.23.3.4.

label: Sentence
text: Where the roof framing on opposite sides of the peak is assembled separately, such as in the case of factory-built houses, the roof framing on opposite sides is permitted to be fastened together with galvanized-steel strips not less than 200 mm by 75 mm by 0.41 mm thick spaced not more than 1.2 m apart and nailed at each end to the framing by at least two 63 mm nails.

label: Article
text: Shaping of Rafters

label: Sentence
text: Rafters shall be shaped at supports to provide even bearing surfaces and supported directly above the exterior walls.

label: Article
text: Hip and Valley Rafters

label: Sentence
text: Hip and valley rafters shall be not less than 50 mm greater in depth than the common rafters and not less than 38 mm thick, actual dimension.

label: Article
text: Intermediate Support for Rafters and Joists

label: Sentence
text: Ceiling joists and collar ties of not less than 38 mm by 89 mm lumber are permitted to be assumed to provide intermediate support to reduce the span for rafters and joists where the roof slope is 1 in 3 or greater.

label: Sentence
text: Collar ties referred to in Sentence (1) more than 2.4 m long shall be laterally supported near their centres by not less than 19 mm by 89 mm continuous members at right angles to the collar ties.

label: Sentence
text: Dwarf walls and struts are permitted to be used to provide intermediate support to reduce the span for rafters and joists.

label: Sentence
text: When struts are used to provide intermediate support they shall be not less than 38 mm by 89 mm material extending from each rafter to a loadbearing wall at an angle of not less than 45° to the horizontal.

label: Article
text: Restraint of Joist Bottoms

label: Sentence
text: Roof joists supporting a finished ceiling, other than plywood, OSB or waferboard, shall be restrained from twisting along the bottom edges by means of furring, blocking, cross bridging or strapping conforming to Article 9.23.9.3.

label: Article
text: Ceiling Joists Supporting Roof Load

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), ceiling joists supporting part of the roof load from the rafters shall be not less than 25 mm greater in depth than required for ceiling joists not supporting part of the roof load.

label: Sentence
text: When the roof slope is 1 in 4 or less, the ceiling joist sizes referred to in Sentence (1) shall be determined from Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-C to 9.23.4.2.-F and 9.23.4.2.-L for roof joists.

label: Article
text: Roof Trusses

label: Sentence
text: Wood roof trusses shall be designed in accordance with good engineering practice such as that described in TPIC 2019, “Truss Design Procedures and Specifications for Light Metal Plate Connected Wood Trusses.”

label: Sentence
text: The joint connections used in trusses described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in conformance with the requirements in Subsection 4.3.1. (See Note A-9.23.14.11.(2).)

label: Sentence
text: All member bracing shall be installed as per the truss design drawings, and continuous lateral bracing shall be adequately anchored to the roof and ceiling diaphragms at intervals no greater than 6.10 m o.c.

label: Article

label: Sentence

text: Application

text: This Section applies to sheet steel studs for use in non- loadbearing exterior and interior walls.

text: Where loadbearing steel studs are used, they shall be designed in conformance with Part 4.

text: Steel studs and runners shall conform to AISI S201, “North American Standard for Cold-Formed Steel Framing - Product Data 2012 Edition.”

text: Metal thickness specified in this Section shall be the minimum base steel thickness exclusive of coatings.

text: Installation of Runners

label: Sentence
text: Runners shall be provided at the tops and bottoms of walls.

text: Runners required in Sentence (1) shall be securely attached to the building at approximately 50 mm from the ends, and at intervals of not more than 600 mm o.c. for interior walls and 300 mm o.c. for exterior walls.

text: Fasteners used for attachment described in Sentence (2) shall consist of the equivalent of 63 mm nails or 25 mm screws.

label: Sentence
text: Studs at openings and which are not full wall height shall be supported by a runner at the ends of the studs, securely fastened to the full length studs at the sides of the opening.

label: Article
text: Fire-Rated Walls

label: Sentence
text: Steel studs used in walls required to have a fire-resistance rating shall be installed so that there is not less than a 12 mm clearance between the top of the stud and the top of the runner to allow for expansion in the event of fire.

text: Except as provided in Article 9.24.3.6., studs in walls referred to in Sentence (1) shall not be attached to the runners in a manner that will prevent such expansion.

label: Sentence
text: Framing above doors with steel door frames in non- loadbearing fire separations required to have a fire-resistance rating shall consist of 2 runners on the flat fastened back to back. (See Note A-9.24.3.2.(3).)

references.link_text: Fire-resistance rating means the time in minutes or hours that a material or assembly of materials will withstand the passage of flame and the transmission of heat when exposed to fire under specified conditions of test and performance criteria, or as determined by extension or interpretation of information derived therefrom as prescribed in this Code. label: Sentence
text: The upper runner required in Sentence (3) shall be bent at each end to extend upwards not less than 150 mm and fastened to the adjacent studs.

text: A gypsum board filler piece, the width and length of the runner, shall be provided between the door frame referred to in Sentence (3) and the adjacent runner.

label: Article
text: Orientation of Studs

label: Sentence
text: Steel studs shall be installed with webs at right angles to the wall face and, except at openings, shall be continuous for the full wall height.

label: Article
text: Support for Cladding Materials

label: Sentence
text: Corners and intersections of walls shall be constructed to provide support for the cladding materials.

label: Article
text: Framing around Openings

label: Sentence
text: Studs shall be doubled on each side of every opening where such openings involve more than one stud space, and shall be tripled where the openings in exterior walls exceed 2.4 m in width.

label: Sentence
text: Studs described in Sentence (1) shall be fastened together by screws, crimping or welding to act as a single structural unit in resisting transverse loads.

label: Article
text: Attachment of Studs to Runners

label: Sentence
text: Studs shall be attached to runners by screws, crimping or welding around wall openings and elsewhere where necessary to keep the studs in alignment during construction.

label: Sentence
text: Where clearance for expansion is required in Article 9.24.3.2., attachment required in Sentence (1) shall be applied between studs and bottom runners only.

label: Article
text: Openings for Fire Dampers

label: Sentence
text: Openings for fire dampers in non- loadbearing fire separations required to have a fire-resistance rating shall be framed with double studs on each side of the opening.

references.link_text: Fire-resistance rating means the time in minutes or hours that a material or assembly of materials will withstand the passage of flame and the transmission of heat when exposed to fire under specified conditions of test and performance criteria, or as determined by extension or interpretation of information derived therefrom as prescribed in this Code. label: Sentence
text: The sill and header for openings described in Sentence (1) shall consist of a runner track with right angle bends made on each end so as to extend 300 mm above the header or below the sill and fastened to the studs.

text: The openings described in Sentence (1) shall be lined with a layer of gypsum board not less than 12.7 mm thick fastened to stud and runner webs.

text: Scope and Application

label: Sentence
text: This Section is concerned with heat, air and water vapour transfer and measures to control condensation.

label: Sentence
text: All walls, ceilings and floors separating conditioned space from unconditioned space, the exterior air or the ground shall be

references.link_text: Conditioned space means any space within a building , the temperature of which is controlled to limit variation in response to the exterior ambient temperature by the provision, either directly or indirectly, of heating or cooling over substantial portions of the year.

title: a)
text: provided with

label: Sentence
text: Insulation and sealing of heating and ventilating ducts shall conform to Sections 9.32., 9.33. and 9.36.

text: Thermal Insulation

label: Article
text: Required Insulation

label: Sentence
text: All walls, ceilings and floors separating heated space from unheated space, the exterior air or the exterior soil shall be provided with sufficient thermal insulation to prevent moisture condensation on their room side during the winter and to ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants. (See Note A-9.1.1.1.(1).)

label: Sentence
text: Except as permitted by Sentence (3) and required by Sentence (4), insulation conforming with Table 9.25.2.1. shall be provided for attached garages and heated detached garages serving a building of residential occupancy . (See Note A-9.25.2.1.(2).)

label: Sentence
text: The flame-spread ratings requirements contained in the standards listed in Sentence (1) shall not apply. (See Note A-9.25.2.2.(2).)

label: Sentence
text: Insulation in contact with the ground shall be inert to the action of soil and water and shall be such that its insulative properties are not significantly reduced by moisture.

references.link_text: Soil means that portion of the earth's crust that is fragmentary, or such that some individual particles of a dried sample may be readily separated by agitation in water; it includes boulders, cobbles, gravel, sand, silt, clay and organic matter.

label: Article
text: Installation of Thermal Insulation

label: Sentence
text: Insulation shall be installed so that there is a reasonably uniform insulating value over the entire face of the insulated area.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation shall be applied to the full width and length of the space between furring or framing.

label: Sentence
text: Except where the insulation provides the principal resistance to air leakage, thermal insulation shall be installed so that at least one face is in full and continuous contact with an element with low air permeance. (See Note A-9.25.2.3.(3).)

label: Sentence
text: Insulation shall be installed over the full height of foundation walls enclosing a basement or heated crawl space. (See also Note A-9.36.2.5.(5).)

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .
Basement means a storey or storeys of a building located below the first storey .

label: Sentence
text: Insulation around concrete slabs-on-ground shall be located so that heat from the building is not restricted from reaching the ground beneath the perimeter, where exterior walls are not supported by footings extending below frost level.

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Sentence
text: Where insulation is exposed to the weather and subject to mechanical damage, it shall be protected with not less than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 6 mm preservative-treated plywood, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 12 mm cement parging on wire lath applied to the exposed face and edge.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation located in areas where it may be subject to mechanical damage shall be protected by a covering such as gypsum board, plywood, particleboard, OSB, waferboard or hardboard.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation in factory-built buildings shall be installed so that it will not become dislodged during transportation.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation shields shall be installed around chimneys and gas vents to ensure that appropriate clearances are maintained when insulation is used in attics.

label: Sentence
text: Insulation shields required in Sentence (9) shall be constructed of noncombustible material of sufficient thickness so that they will not be deformed during installation and shall be designed so that the appropriate clearance is maintained automatically.

references.link_text: Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Article
text: Installation of Loose-Fill Insulation

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) to (6), loose-fill insulation shall be used on horizontal surfaces only.

label: Sentence
text: Where loose-fill insulation is installed in an unconfined sloped space, such as an attic space over a sloped ceiling, the supporting slope shall not be more than

label: Clause
title: a)
text: 4.5 in 12 for mineral fibre or cellulose fibre insulation, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: 2.5 in 12 for other types of insulation.

label: Sentence
text: Loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used in wood-frame walls of existing buildings . (See Note A-9.25.2.4.(3).)

label: Sentence
text: Where blown-in insulation is installed in above-ground or below-ground wood-frame walls of new buildings ,

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the density of the installed insulation shall be sufficient to preclude settlement,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: the insulation shall be installed behind a membrane that will permit visual inspection prior to the installation of the interior finish,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: the insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not interfere with the installation of the interior finish, and

label: Clause
title: d)
text: no water shall be added to the insulation, unless it can be shown that the added water will not adversely affect other materials in the assembly.

label: Sentence
text: Water repellent loose-fill insulation is permitted to be used between the outer and inner wythes of masonry cavity walls . (See Note A-9.25.2.4.(5).)

label: Sentence
text: Where soffit venting is used, measures shall be taken

label: Clause
title: a)
text: to prevent loose-fill insulation from blocking the soffit vents and to maintain an open path for circulation of air from the vents into the attic or roof space , and

references.link_text: Attic or roof space means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

label: Clause
title: b)
text: to minimize airflow into the insulation near the soffit vents to maintain the thermal performance of the material. (See Article 9.19.1.3.)

label: Article
text: Installation of Spray-Applied Polyurethane

label: Sentence
text: Spray-applied polyurethane insulation shall be installed in accordance with CAN/ULC-S705.2, “Standard for Thermal Insulation – Spray Applied Rigid Polyurethane Foam, Medium Density – Application.”

label: Subsection
text: Air Barrier Systems

label: Article
text: Required Barrier to Air Leakage

label: Sentence
text: Wall, ceiling and floor assemblies separating conditioned space from unconditioned space or from the ground shall be constructed so as to include an air barrier system that will provide a continuous barrier to air leakage

references.link_text: Conditioned space means any space within a building , the temperature of which is controlled to limit variation in response to the exterior ambient temperature by the provision, either directly or indirectly, of heating or cooling over substantial portions of the year.

label: Clause
title: a)
text: from the interior of the building into wall, floor, attic or roof spaces , sufficient to prevent excessive moisture condensation in such spaces during the winter, and

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: from the exterior or the ground inward sufficient to

label: Subclause
title: i)
text: prevent moisture condensation on the room side during winter,

label: Subclause
title: ii)
text: ensure comfortable conditions for the occupants, and

label: Clause
title: iii) minimize the ingress of
text: soil gas.

references.link_text: Soil means that portion of the earth's crust that is fragmentary, or such that some individual particles of a dried sample may be readily separated by agitation in water; it includes boulders, cobbles, gravel, sand, silt, clay and organic matter.

label: Article
text: Air Barrier System Properties

label: Sentence
text: Air barrier systems shall possess the characteristics necessary to provide an effective barrier to air infiltration and exfiltration under differential air pressure due to stack effect, mechanical systems or wind.

label: Sentence
text: Where polyethylene sheet is used to provide airtightness in the air barrier system , it shall conform to CAN/CGSB-51.34-M, “Vapour Barrier, Polyethylene Sheet for Use in Building Construction.”

label: Article
text: Continuity of the Air Barrier System

label: Sentence
text: Where the air barrier system consists of an air-impermeable panel-type material, all joints shall be sealed to prevent air leakage.

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence 9.25.3.6.(3), where the air barrier system consists of flexible sheet material, all joints shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: sealed, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: lapped not less than 100 mm and clamped, such as between framing members, furring or blocking, and rigid panels.

label: Sentence
text: Where an interior wall meets an exterior wall, ceiling, floor or roof required to be provided with air barrier protection, the air barrier system shall extend across the intersection.

label: Sentence
text: Where an interior wall projects through a ceiling or extends to become an exterior wall, spaces in the wall shall be blocked to provide continuity across those spaces with the air barrier system in the abutting walls or ceiling.

label: Sentence
text: Where an interior floor projects through an exterior wall or extends to become an exterior floor, continuity of the air barrier system shall be maintained from the abutting walls across the floor assembly.

label: Sentence
text: Penetrations of the air barrier system , such as those created by the installation of doors, windows, electrical wiring, electrical boxes, piping or ductwork, shall be sealed to maintain the integrity of the air barrier system over the entire surface.

label: Sentence
text: Where access hatches and sump pit covers are installed through assemblies constructed with an air barrier system , they shall be weatherstripped around their perimeters to prevent air leakage.

label: Sentence
text: Clearances between chimneys or gas vents and the surrounding construction that would permit air leakage from within the building into a wall or attic or roof space shall be sealed by noncombustible material to prevent such leakage.

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,
Attic or roof space means the space between the roof and the ceiling of the top storey or between a dwarf wall and a sloping roof.

Noncombustible means that a material meets the acceptance criteria of CAN/ULC-S114, “Standard Method of Test for Determination of Non-Combustibility in Building Materials.” Noncombustible construction means that type of construction in which a degree of fire safety is attained by the use of noncombustible materials for structural members and other building assemblies.

label: Article
text: Air Leakage Control in Masonry Walls

label: Sentence
text: Masonry walls required to provide a barrier to the ingress of air from the ground shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: include a course of masonry units without voids, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: be sealed with flashing material extending across the full width of the masonry.

label: Sentence
text: The masonry course or flashing described in Sentence (1) shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: be located at the level of the adjoining floor and be sealed to it in accordance with Article 9.25.3.6., or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: in the absence of a floor, be located at the level of the ground cover required by Article 9.18.6.1. and be sealed to it.

label: Article
text: Air Leakage Control in Underground Roofs

label: Sentence
text: Waterproofing systems for roofs of underground structures shall be sealed to the air barrier in the walls.

label: Article
text: Air Barrier Systems in Floors-on-ground

label: Sentence
text: Materials used to provide a barrier to the ingress of air through floors-on-ground shall conform to CAN/CGSB-51.34-M, “Vapour Barrier, Polyethylene Sheet for Use in Building Construction.”

label: Sentence
text: Where the floor-on-ground is a concrete slab, the air barrier shall be

label: Clause
title: a)
text: installed below the slab, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: applied to the top of the slab, provided a separate floor is installed over the slab.

label: Sentence
text: Where the air barrier installed below a floor-on-ground is flexible sheet material, joints in the barrier shall be lapped not less than 300 mm. (See Note A-9.25.3.6.(2) and (3).)

label: Sentence
text: Where installed in conjunction with a framed floor-on-ground or above a floor-on-ground, the air barrier shall be installed in accordance with Article 9.25.3.3.

label: Sentence
text: A floor-on-ground shall be sealed around its perimeter to the inner surfaces of adjacent walls using flexible sealant.

label: Sentence
text: All penetrations of a floor-on-ground that are required to drain water from the floor surface shall be sealed in a manner that prevents the upward flow of air without preventing the downward flow of liquid water.

label: Subsection
text: Vapour Barriers

label: Article
text: Required Barrier to Vapour Diffusion

label: Sentence
text: Thermally insulated wall, ceiling and floor assemblies shall be constructed with a vapour barrier so as to provide a barrier to diffusion of water vapour from the interior into wall spaces, floor spaces or attic or roof spaces .

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Article
text: Vapour Barrier Materials

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), vapour barriers shall have a permeance not greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m 2 ) measured in accordance with ASTM E96/E96M, “Standard Test Methods for Water Vapor Transmission of Materials,” using the desiccant method (dry cup).

label: Sentence
text: Thermally insulated foundation wall assemblies are permitted to be constructed with variable-permeance vapour barriers having a permeance not greater than 60 ng/(Pa×s×m 2 ) using the desiccant method (dry cup) and greater than 300 ng/(Pa×s×m 2 ) using the water method (wet cup) measured in accordance with ASTM E96/E96M, “Standard Test Methods for Water Vapor Transmission of Materials.”(See Note A-9.25.4.2.(2).)

references.link_text: Foundation means a system or arrangement of foundation units through which the loads from a building are transferred to supporting soil or rock .

label: Sentence
text: Where the intended use of the interior space will result in high moisture generation, the assembly shall be designed according to Part 5. (See Note A-9.25.4.2.(3).)

label: Sentence
text: Where polyethylene is installed to serve only as the vapour barrier , it shall comply with Clause 4.4, Thermal Stability, and Clause 5.7, Oxidative Induction Time, of CAN/CGSB-51.34-M, “Vapour Barrier, Polyethylene Sheet for Use in Building Construction.”

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Sentence
text: Membrane-type vapour barriers other than polyethylene shall conform to the requirements of CAN/CGSB-51.33-M, “Vapour Barrier Sheet, Excluding Polyethylene, for Use in Building Construction.”

label: Sentence
text: Membrane-type vapour barriers other than polyethylene that are susceptible to deterioration under prolonged exposure to direct ultraviolet radiation shall

label: Clause
title: a)
text: be covered, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: only be installed in locations that are not exposed to direct ultraviolet radiation after the completion of construction.

label: Sentence
text: Where a coating is applied to gypsum board to function as the vapour barrier , the permeance of the coating shall be determined in accordance with CAN/CGSB-1.501-M, “Method for Permeance of Coated Wallboard.”

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Sentence
text: Where foamed plastic insulation functions as the vapour barrier , it shall be sufficiently thick so as to meet the requirement of Sentence (1).

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Article
text: Installation of Vapour Barriers

label: Sentence
text: Products installed to function as the vapour barrier shall protect the warm side of wall, ceiling and floor assemblies.

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Sentence
text: Where different products are used for the vapour barrier and the insulation, the vapour barrier shall be installed sufficiently close to the warm side of the insulation to prevent condensation at design conditions. (See Notes A-9.25.4.3.(2) and A-9.25.5.1.(1).)

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.
Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Sentence
text: Where the same product is used for the vapour barrier and the insulation, the product shall be installed sufficiently close to the warm side of the assembly to prevent condensation at design conditions. (See Notes A-9.25.4.3.(2), A-9.25.5.1.(1) and A-9.25.5.2.)

references.link_text: Vapour barrier means the elements installed to control the diffusion of water vapour.

label: Section
title: Section 9.26.
text: Roofing

label: Subsection
text: General

label: Article
text: Definitions

label: Sentence
text: For the purpose of this Section, the term “roof” shall mean sloped or near-horizontal assemblies that protect the spaces beneath them, including platforms that effectively serve as roofs with respect to the accumulation or drainage of precipitation. (See Note A-9.26.1.1.(1).)

label: Sentence
text: For the purpose of this Section, the term “roofing” shall mean the primary covering for roofs.

label: Article
text: Required Protection

label: Sentence
text: Roofs shall be protected with roofing, including flashing, installed so as to

label: Clause
title: a)
text: effectively shed water,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: prevent the ingress of water and moisture into building assemblies and occupied space, and

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Clause
title: c)
text: minimize the ingress of water due to ice damming into building assemblies.

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Sentence
text: Compliance with Sentence (1) shall be demonstrated by conforming to

label: Clause
title: a)
text: the remainder of this Section, or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: Part 5.

label: Article
text: Alternative Installation Methods

label: Sentence
text: Methods described in CSA A123.51, “Asphalt shingle application on roof slopes 1:6 and steeper,” are permitted to be used for the installation of asphalt shingles in lieu of the methods described in this Section.

label: Article
text: Installation of Materials

label: Sentence
text: Materials listed in Tables 9.26.2.1.-A and 9.26.2.1.-B shall be installed in conformance with the manufacturer's written instructions. (See Sentence 1.5.1.2.(1) of Division A.)

label: Article
text: Nails

label: Sentence
text: Nails used for roofing shall be corrosion-resistant roofing or shingle nails conforming to

label: Clause
title: a)
text: ASTM F1667, “Standard Specification for Driven Fasteners: Nails, Spikes, and Staples,” or

label: Clause
title: b)
text: CSA B111, “Wire Nails, Spikes and Staples.”

label: Sentence
text: Nails shall have sufficient length to penetrate through, or 12 mm into, roof sheathing.

label: Sentence
text: Nails used with asphalt roofing shall have a head diameter of not less than 9.5 mm and a shank thickness of not less than 2.95 mm.

label: Sentence
text: Nails used with wood shingles or shakes shall have a head diameter of not less than 4.8 mm and a shank thickness of not less than 2.0 mm and shall be stainless steel, aluminum or hot-dipped galvanized. (See Note A-9.26.2.3.(4).)

label: Article
text: Staples

label: Sentence
text: Staples used to apply asphalt or wood shingles shall be corrosion-resistant and shall be driven with the crown parallel to the eaves.

label: Sentence
text: Staples used with asphalt shingles shall be not less than 19 mm long, 1.6 mm diam or thickness, with not less than a 25 mm crown, except that an 11 mm crown may be used as provided in Sentence 9.26.7.4.(2).

label: Sentence
text: Staples used with wood shingles shall be not less than 29 mm long, 1.6 mm diam or thickness, with not less than a 9.5 mm crown and shall be stainless steel or aluminum. (See Note A-9.26.2.3.(4).)

label: Subsection
text: Slope of Roofed Surfaces

label: Article
text: Slope

label: Sentence
text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3), the slopes on which roof coverings may be applied shall conform to Table 9.26.3.1.

label: Sentence
text: Asphalt and gravel or coal tar and gravel roofs may be constructed with lower slopes than required in Sentence (1) when effective drainage is provided by roof drains located at the lowest points on the roofs.

label: Sentence
text: Profiled metal roof cladding systems specifically designed for low-slope applications are permitted to be installed with lower slopes than required by Sentence (1), provided they are installed in conformance with the manufacturer's written recommendations.

label: Sentence
text: Except where back-slope will not adversely affect adjacent supported or supporting constructions due to water ingress, roofs and constructions that effectively serve as roofs shall be constructed with sufficient slope away from

label: Clause
title: a)
text: exterior walls, and

label: Clause
title: b)
text: guards that are connected to the roof, or to a construction that effectively serves as a roof, by more than pickets or posts.

label: Sentence
text: The slope required by Sentence (4) shall be sufficient to maintain a positive slope

label: Clause
title: a)
text: after expected shrinkage of the building frame, where these surfaces are supported by exterior walls and exterior columns (see Note A-9.27.3.8.(4)), and

references.link_text: building , condominium, multiple housing unit, residential development, private educational institution or private club, the use of which is restricted entirely to the registered guests, owners, tenants, students or members, as the case may be, and their guests,

label: Clause
title: b)
text: once design loading is taken into consideration, where these surfaces are cantilevered from exterior walls.
